entities.name: The Transformation
entities.tagline: At 2:23 in the morning on January 3rd, every building on the planet came down at once, and almost everyone who was indoors died.

beats.headline: January 3rd, and then the announcement
beats.text: It is over in an instant: every building crushed flat at once. Then a voice speaks planet-wide: the dungeon has eighteen levels, and completing the last returns the planet from the Borant Corporation's regency. The entrances open. The survivors are, near enough without exception, the people who happened to be standing outside — at two in the morning in a Seattle cold snap, almost nobody.
beats.gist: Every building is crushed flat, and a voice announces eighteen levels to reclaim the planet from Borant Corporation.

beats.headline: Thirteen million go down the stairs
beats.text: Midway through the tutorial the announcement comes: just under thirteen million made it through the gates, and already fewer than ten million are left.
beats.gist: Just under thirteen million people enter the gates, but fewer than ten million remain.

recap.text: Every building is crushed flat at once. A voice announces a dungeon with eighteen levels, and completing the last returns the planet from the Borant Corporation's regency. Just under thirteen million people enter the gates in a Seattle cold snap, and fewer than ten million remain by midway through the tutorial.

tagline.text: The dungeon has eighteen levels, and whoever completes the last one wins the planet back from the Borant Corporation's regency.
Every floor runs on a timer, and when it expires, the floor collapses with everyone still on it.

beats.headline: The terms
beats.text: Reach the bottom and humanity gets Earth back. Most crawlers do not make it past the tenth floor. Every floor collapses when its timer runs out, and the timers are set by ratings and how many crawlers are left, usually about five days longer than the last.
beats.gist: Humanity gets Earth back if crawlers reach the bottom, but most fail before the tenth floor.

beats.headline: Under a million
beats.text: On the recap Le Mouvement is gone to a city boss, all but one man, and the ticker reads 990,303. Carl had not noticed it drop below a million, and for every crawler that ticks away he feels a part of himself going with them.
beats.gist: Le Mouvement is gone to a city boss except for one man; the ticker reads 990,303.

beats.headline: The cliff at the fourth floor
beats.text: The early floors are built to bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. Past the third floor, achievements are harder to come by.
beats.gist: Early floors bury crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills, but achievements harden past the third floor.

beats.headline: The clock, from the other side
beats.text: The goblin shamanka Rory explains how a collapse looks to a mob. Mobs cannot leave their floor: start down the stairs and the body dissolves halfway, she has seen it. When the floor goes, only crawlers die. Mobs sleep until the next dungeon opens and wake to the same day. The promise is that one day they will wake deeper, and one day deep enough that crawlers never come, with peace and a place to raise their little ones. Kill the crawlers, get better at killing, and you get to go deeper. That is what they are told.
beats.gist: Rory the goblin shamanka explains that mobs dissolve if they leave their floor.

beats.headline: Two million, five hundred and fifty-two thousand
beats.text: The number on the screen reads 2,552,085. From thirteen million to this, in just under four days. Every one of those digits was somebody. The third episode spends its second half on five groups, among them Lucia Mar and a woman with a magical crossbow, who have found their stairwells already and are camping beside them, waiting for the clock to reach exactly six hours.
beats.gist: The screen reads 2,552,085, and five groups, including Lucia Mar, camp beside their stairwells.

beats.headline: A third of the crawlers, in one rumble
beats.text: The first-floor timer runs out as the episode starts. The ground shakes for a second and the count drops from just over two million to 1,292,526: more than seven hundred thousand dead at once, a third of those left. The first floor took a little more than ten million. The second floor's clock resets to six days, because the count is below projections and six is the minimum the rules allow. Borant urges everyone to wait until the last possible moment to descend.
beats.gist: The first-floor timer runs out and the count drops to 1,292,526, killing over seven hundred thousand.

beats.headline: Eight days for the third
beats.text: Halfway through Carl's class selection the world rumbles: the second floor has collapsed. Just over 700,000 crawlers remain, and the third floor gets eight full days. Mordecai does the arithmetic out loud. If they keep this up, the sixth floor will be open only eleven or twelve days, where it is usually open for thirty, and the factions are going to be pissed.
beats.gist: The second floor collapses, leaving 700,000 crawlers and giving the third floor eight full days.

beats.headline: Where the tourists are
beats.text: No tourists on the third floor, Mordecai says. Most of them are on the eighteenth, a billionaire's luxury retreat where the galaxy's rich and elite party, gamble and satiate their most base desires, and the one place where printed people may legally be used for the rest. Carl asks what happens if a crawler gets there. Nobody ever has, so nobody knows; the same goes for the fifteenth. Borant and the AI are required to have a plan.
beats.gist: Mordecai says billionaires party and gamble on the eighteenth floor where printed people are legally used.

beats.headline: The clock is suspended
beats.text: Winner, sort of: neither boss is dead, and the AI calls it anyway. The door on the eighteenth floor is open. Then a system message: all level collapse timers past the eleventh floor are suspended until a winner is declared in the Ascendency battles, at which point dungeon closure begins. The floors below are no longer on a timer. The Ascendency is.
beats.gist: The AI declares a winner without a dead boss, opening the eighteenth floor door.

recap.text: Humanity gets Earth back if they reach the bottom, but most do not pass the tenth floor. Floors collapse when timers run out, killing only crawlers. The first-floor timer ends and the count drops to 1,292,526. The second floor's clock resets to six days because the count is below projections.

The world rumbles during Carl's class selection and the second floor collapses. Mordecai calculates that the third floor gets eight full days and the sixth floor may open for only eleven or twelve days. Mordecai says the galaxy's rich party and gamble on the eighteenth floor, where printed people are legally used. Borant and the AI must have a plan.

The AI declares a winner while neither boss is dead. The door on the eighteenth floor opens. A system message suspends all level collapse timers past the eleventh floor until a winner is declared in the Ascendency battles. The floors below are no longer on a timer, but the Ascendency is.

entities.name: Dungeon Crawler World
entities.tagline: The crawl is a television programme called Dungeon Crawler World, broadcast across the Syndicate's three billion star systems, and the survivors are its cast.

beats.headline: Ratings are currency
beats.text: Ratings buy sponsors, sponsors send gold and loot, and loot buys another floor. Being watchable is a survival stat, and even the floor timers are set partly by ratings.
beats.gist: Ratings buy sponsors who send gold and loot to buy another floor.

beats.headline: The first episode airs
beats.text: The crawlers get to watch themselves. Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug in the same breath.
beats.gist: The crawlers watch themselves as Borant patches the hallway bathroom bug.

beats.headline: There are other shows
beats.text: Zev introduces herself as the liaison between Borant and the privately run programmes that borrow crawlers for their own shows. A production may pluck a crawler off between stairwells; anything else goes through her office. A crawler may turn a show down, but has to pick one.
beats.gist: Zev liaises between Borant and private shows that borrow crawlers between stairwells.

beats.headline: Viewers may now read the chat
beats.text: The second-to-last message of the floor opens with pride in human tenacity: fewer deaths than expected, which has them rethinking how easy the next floor was going to be. Crawlers on the next floor will be scattered further apart, and only parties formed before the message began will travel together, so goodbyes are best said now. For a small fee, viewers may now subscribe to the private messages between crawlers, live the moment the message ends. And liquids may no longer be stored in an inventory unless they are in a container.
beats.gist: Viewers read a chat message about human tenacity, crawler scattering, private message subscriptions, and liquid storage.

beats.headline: Fifty to one
beats.text: A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event: viewers where betting is legal wager on outcomes general and specific, at odds the AI sets. It put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and plenty of viewers took the bet. Borant has filed an appeal against the odds, citing the AI's sluggishness in moving the spread; nobody yet knows how much it lost. Minutes after, a new snick, Carl's Naughty Little Piggie Goes to Market, is doing the rounds. The showrunners will not let it be shown.
beats.gist: A Death Challenge is a gambling event where viewers wager on outcomes at AI-set odds.

beats.headline: Viewing is mandatory
beats.text: Every screen everywhere except the center system shows the same feed: a map of the tunnel nodes, then Earth, zooming in on the Pacific about three hundred miles off Washington State, then a long, mostly straight road paved with yellow bricks through endless grass. Then a countdown, and two lines. The Parade Begins soon. Viewing is mandatory. Zev has no idea where it is coming from.
beats.gist: Every screen outside the center system shows a map of tunnel nodes, Earth, and a yellow brick road.

recap.text: Ratings buy sponsors who send gold and loot to buy another floor. Borant patches a hallway bathroom bug as the crawlers watch their first episode. Zev acts as a liaison between Borant and private programmes that borrow crawlers for shows. A crawler may turn a show down but must pick one.

The second-to-last message of the floor notes fewer deaths than expected and warns that crawlers will be scattered further apart. Viewers may pay a fee to subscribe to private messages between crawlers, and liquids now require a container for inventory storage. A Death Challenge pop-up gambling event sets Carl's survival at fifty to one. Borant appeals the odds, and showrunners block a snick called Carl's Naughty Little Piggie Goes to Market.

Every screen except the center system shows a map of tunnel nodes, Earth, the Pacific three hundred miles off Washington State, and a yellow brick road through grass. A countdown and two lines appear. The Parade Begins soon and viewing is mandatory. Zev does not know where the feed comes from.

entities.name: The Recap
entities.tagline: The recap plays on the safe-room screens, narrated by an orange, four-eyed, lizard-like creature. The premiere is mostly about last season, and it has no time at all for Donut's boss fight.

beats.headline: It introduces you to your rivals
beats.text: The third recap brings in a hundred and fifty armed men from Africa, and then a boss battle. Whole factions arrive in the story as segments.
beats.gist: The third recap brings one hundred and fifty armed men from Africa and a boss battle.

beats.headline: Special Edition: the races
beats.text: A special edition shows what the favourite crawlers chose. First a demon-like city boss with crab pincers kills about forty crawlers in seconds. Then Hekla, a man who became a massive slug, a four-armed Kabaddi Raider, Carl, Donut, and Lucia Mar to close. Just about 80 per cent of crawlers have stayed human. A clip of an old Primal with wispy angel wings and a lightning sword, charging a twelfth-floor Divine Guardian, fades before the fight. Mordecai says he died a minute afterwards.
beats.gist: A special edition shows favorite crawlers, including a crab-pincered city boss and a slug-man named Hekla.

beats.headline: Fifteen seconds of Mongo
beats.text: The recap airs a fifteen-second montage of Mongo guarding a sleeping Donut, killing dozens of street urchins. Carl gets a few seconds and no explanation of how he got out of the circus: that scene belongs to the Vengeance of the Daughter production, Mordecai says, and anyone looking at Carl's numbers already knows. The same episode is following a crawler with an alligator head and a mag-fed shotgun that never seems to need reloading. Donut wants to know how he gets a T-shirt over that head.
beats.gist: The recap airs Mongo killing street urchins while Donut sleeps; Donut questions an alligator-headed crawler's T-shirt.

beats.headline: The board, two hours in
beats.text: Elle, Li Jun, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam Dom, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia Mar, all in one broadcast. It is how the crawl keeps track of itself.
beats.gist: Elle, Li Jun, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam Dom, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia Mar appear in one broadcast.

beats.headline: A tribute to Hekla
beats.text: The whole recap is a tribute to the death of Hekla. It opens on her walking in, in street clothes, fighting with a husband who looks twenty years older; she leaves him poisoned by a cactus and comes back to find rats eating him, and kills one with his rib for a Legendary Grrl Power box. It shows Eva killing the man who grabbed Katia, and Eva leaving character creation on the third floor while Katia was still transforming. Then the plough, and Katia killing Hekla, cut as rage at being used rather than an accident.
beats.gist: The recap tributes Hekla's death.

beats.headline: Wall climbers and an absence
beats.text: The recap features the fight on the falling house. Prepotente and Miriam Dom are as far along as Carl's party: they scaled their bubble's inner wall, sent every spider plummeting in its sleep, finished the subterranean zone with it, and are preparing to go underwater. Lucia Mar shatters a multi-limbed ice mummy and is working with a group. Quan Ch has already popped his bubble and is flying around farming every mob he can find. The top ten: Lucia Mar first, Carl second, Prepotente third, Donut fourth. Florin the crocodilian has dropped off it.
beats.gist: The recap shows the fight on the falling house and the current top ten rankings.

beats.headline: Almost entirely redacted
beats.text: Almost the whole recap is redacted. What survives: an undead Easter Bunny stuffing crawlers' limbs into plastic eggs; a group in Tokyo chased by a sentient umbrella and wiped out by a bus; Elle beating a sasquatch half to death and flagging it; Prepotente flagging a giant bat single-handed. Then a studio with faces in little boxes, and nothing, for almost an hour. Mordecai spots a gleener beside Kevin: Prime Minister Glory, boss of the entire Syndicate, who very rarely appears on the show. Afterwards the top ten barely moves.
beats.gist: The recap is redacted except for an undead Easter Bunny, a sentient umbrella, and flagging feats.

recap.text: The third recap introduces a hundred and fifty armed men from Africa. A boss battle follows. Whole factions arrive in the story as segments.

A special edition shows a city boss with crab pincers kill forty crawlers. Hekla, a massive slug, a four-armed Kabaddi Raider, Carl, Donut, and Lucia Mar appear. A clip of an old Primal with angel wings and a lightning sword fades before he dies. A montage shows Mongo killing street urchins while Donut sleeps. A crawler with an alligator head and a mag-fed shotgun appears, and Donut wonders how he wears a T-shirt.

The broadcast keeps track of the crawl through Elle, Li Jun, Ifechi, Florin, Miriam Dom, Prepotente, Hekla and Lucia Mar. A tribute to the death of Hekla shows her leaving a husband poisoned by a cactus and killing a rat with his rib for a Legendary Grrl Power box. Eva kills a man who grabbed Katia and leaves character creation while Katia transforms. Katia kills Hekla with a plough.

The recap shows a fight on a falling house. Prepotente and Miriam Dom scaled their bubble's inner wall and sent every spider plummeting in its sleep. Lucia Mar shatters a multi-limbed ice mummy. Quan Ch popped his bubble and flies around farming every mob. Lucia Mar is first in the top ten, followed by Carl, Prepotente, and Donut, while Florin the crocodilian dropped off.

Most of the recap is redacted. Surviving images show an undead Easter Bunny stuffing limbs into plastic eggs, a sentient umbrella chasing a group in Tokyo before a bus wipes them out, Elle beating and flagging a sasquatch, and Prepotente flagging a giant bat. Prime Minister Glory, boss of the Syndicate, appears as a gleener beside Kevin. The top ten barely moves.

tagline.text: Carl has been given several of something that sounds a lot like loot boxes. The rat man tells him where they are kept, and then tells him that he cannot get at them yet.
Loot boxes come in six tiers, from bronze to celestial, each far rarer than the last. They open only in a safe room, all of them at once and lowest tier first.

beats.headline: Where they come from, and how they open
beats.text: Achievements, mostly, and patrons, who alone can send Benefactor Boxes. They stay locked in the Awards and Boxes tab until a safe room or guildhall, and then it is all or nothing — every box you have opens in sequence, lowest tier first, and you cannot pick. Read every description before equipping anything. As Mordecai puts it: always, always, no exceptions.
beats.gist: Achievements and patrons provide loot boxes, which open in sequence from lowest tier in safe rooms.

beats.headline: The top tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on every non-sponsored box it hands out: a handful of free Celestials a season, and a steeper bill for each one after that. In the whole history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have been awarded, and no crawler has had more than four. The previous record for one season was eighteen, in a Naga season long ago.
beats.gist: Borant owes the Syndicate tax on non-sponsored boxes, and only 2,145 Celestial boxes have ever been awarded.

beats.headline: Benefactor Boxes ignore the theme
beats.text: Only patrons can send them, and they are the one kind that will produce a pulse rifle or powered armour in a fantasy dungeon. A Bronze Benefactor Box beats a plain Gold Adventurer Box.
beats.gist: Patrons send Benefactor Boxes that produce pulse rifles or powered armour and beat Gold Adventurer Boxes.

beats.headline: Bully and a Thief
beats.text: The first-floor accounts settle in a French storm shelter. Borough Boss: top five per cent of crawlers, reward "Yeah, no." Bully and a Thief, for taking the old woman's shopping cart: a Bronze Asshole's Box with five gold and three Desperado Club drink tickets, "drink" in quotation marks. Battlefield Construction: a Silver Mechanic's Box and a Goo-Inator 3000 that needs a workbench. You found stairs: the reward is being alive to read it. And for more than five kills in boss fights with bare feet, in the AI's sexy voice, a Platinum Shoe Box.
beats.gist: First-floor accounts settle in a French storm shelter with boxes for specific actions and achievements.

beats.headline: Hadji, and a casino chip
beats.text: Carl and Donut hit a quadrillion views among the first ten crawlers to do it, and each gets a Gold box whose contents the followers vote on, locked for thirty hours. The Hadji achievement, for finishing a quest an unusual way, lifts both their Gold Quest Boxes to Platinum: 5,000 gold each, a skill potion and fang caps for Donut, a Scroll of Upgrade for Carl. His Lucky Bastard box holds a 100,000 gold casino chip, playable only at the Desperado Club's tables. Donut earned the same survival achievement and got no box at all. Nobody knows why.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut hit a quadrillion views and get Gold boxes voted on by followers.

beats.headline: Eighty-three Celestials, and one veto
beats.text: A quest reward gets double-upgraded to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant burns its single seasonal veto to void them and is a moment too slow — Quan Ch has already opened his, which leaves the company liable and in a Syndicate court. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.
beats.gist: Borant burns a seasonal veto too slow to stop Quan Ch from opening double-upgraded Celestial rewards.

beats.headline: A box for every hunter
beats.text: Carl's thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes line up across the room, and each one holds gold, a thousand more than the last, and a severed hand: Xindy's claw first, then the drunk draconian's, then an orc's. Five hundred and ninety-five thousand gold, and not a ring on any of them. The hands are Hunting Trophies. The prize counter that takes them opens at a party called the Butcher's Masquerade near the end of the floor, where the cheapest prize costs a single hand. Sell or transfer one and it reverts to being some dude's appendage.
beats.gist: Carl opens thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes containing five hundred ninety-five thousand gold and severed Hunting Trophies.

beats.headline: Suspiciously good loot
beats.text: After the skipped floor, the feeds fill with crawlers opening very good boxes: an ice staff for Elle, a shape-changing ring for Bautista, a nipple ring and a summoning tome for Donut. Mordecai reads it two ways. Part of it is the AI compensating for the floor nobody got to play. But some of those boxes were earned before the skip, so it is likely a response to the Valtay ramping up the difficulty. More than a thousand crawlers also receive the identical box at the same moment and earn Collective Bargaining, whose citation promises to toughen up the rules.
beats.gist: Crawlers open boxes containing an ice staff, a shape-changing ring, a nipple ring, and a summoning tome.

recap.text: Achievements and patrons provide loot boxes, which stay locked until a safe room or guildhall. Boxes open in sequence from lowest tier first. Benefactor Boxes ignore the theme and can produce a pulse rifle or powered armour. A Bronze Benefactor Box beats a plain Gold Adventurer Box. Rewards for a French storm shelter include a Bronze Asshole's Box with five gold and three drink tickets, a Silver Mechanic's Box, a Goo-Inator 3000, and a Platinum Shoe Box.

Borant owes the Syndicate tax on non-sponsored boxes, and only 2,145 Celestial boxes have been awarded in the show's history. Carl and Donut hit a quadrillion views and receive Gold boxes, which the Hadji achievement upgrades to Platinum. Carl gets a Scroll of Upgrade and a 100,000 gold casino chip for the Desperado Club. Borant uses its single seasonal veto to void Celestial rewards for 83 crawlers, but Quan Ch opens his first.

Carl lines up thirty-four Gold Hunter-Killer boxes. They contain five hundred and ninety-five thousand gold and Hunting Trophies in the form of severed hands, including Xindy's claw, a drunk draconian's, and an orc's. A prize counter at the Butcher's Masquerade takes these hands, though selling or transferring one reverts it to some dude's appendage.

Crawlers open boxes containing an ice staff for Elle, a shape-changing ring for Bautista, and a nipple ring and summoning tome for Donut. Mordecai attributes this to the AI compensating for a skipped floor and the Valtay ramping up difficulty. Over a thousand crawlers receive the same box and earn Collective Bargaining to toughen up the rules.

entities.name: Compensated Anarchist
entities.tagline: Compensated Anarchist is Carl's class, a unique hybrid of monk and rogue: trapmaker, bomb-maker and social-media dynamo, happy to throw a Molotov through a window one moment and to plead on camera for the violence to stop the next.

beats.headline: Taken with the Primal race
beats.text: "The Compensated Anarchist will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next."
beats.gist: The Compensated Anarchist throws a Molotov through a window and then pleads for violence to stop.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The bomb-focused specialisation, taken on the Hunting Grounds.
beats.gist: Carl takes the Agent Provocateur bomb-focused specialisation on the Hunting Grounds.

recap.text: Carl takes the Compensated Anarchist class with the Primal race. This class throws a Molotov through a window and then pleads for the violence to stop in front of a camera.
Carl takes the Agent Provocateur specialisation on the Hunting Grounds. This specialisation focuses on bombs.

entities.name: Former Child Actor
entities.tagline: Former Child Actor is Donut's class, a hybrid of bard and rogue built on charisma and chance. On every floor she picks a new specialty, and the AI decides how much of it she gets.

beats.headline: Taken with the Cat race
beats.text: Donut picks it while pretending to pick something else, and takes Artist Alley Mogul as her first specialty. It is a Charisma-and-chance class built on the Character Actor skill: each floor she chooses a specialty, the AI rolls how much of that class she gets, and when the floor ends she loses it and starts over. Her own spells are untouched. It also makes her immune to poison and disease and hands her Cockroach, a chance to survive a killing blow.
beats.gist: Donut picks the Cat race and the Artist Alley Mogul specialty.

recap.text: Donut picks the Cat race and the Artist Alley Mogul specialty. Her class relies on the Character Actor skill, which requires the AI to roll how much of a chosen specialty she receives each floor before she loses it. The class makes her immune to poison and disease and gives her Cockroach to survive a killing blow.

entities.name: The Desperado Club
entities.tagline: The Desperado Pass is a tattoo, branded onto Donut's shoulder blade and Carl's neck, and it grants access to the Desperado Club. What the club actually is, the description does not say.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: Carl and Donut are both branded with the Desperado Pass out of their Asshole Boxes in a first-floor safe room — his on the neck, hers on the right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. Donut is appalled.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut receive glowing gold Desperado Pass tattoos from their Asshole Boxes in a safe room.

beats.headline: The members-only room
beats.text: The front room is for locals and crawlers still earning a pass. Past Clarabelle is the members' floor, and it sits on its own plane: every club location on the level opens into the same room, and a member leaves through the door they came in by. Most of the crowd are bots, one vanishing whenever a real visitor arrives. A drawn halo gives a privacy bubble. Doors lead to two brothels, a jobs room, the Silk Road market, and three unlit signs, one of them a casino that is not open yet.
beats.gist: The members-only room sits on its own plane and connects every club location on the level.

beats.headline: The bait is a job at the club
beats.text: Burgundy worked in another settlement until city elves told her she could get a job at the Desperado Club, which had an entrance in this town. Everyone knows, she says, that working at the club brings a chance to descend, and maybe deeper, where it's safe. It was all a lie. Women who come to work at the club are the ones brought to Remex.
beats.gist: City elves told Burgundy she could work at the Desperado Club to descend to safety.

beats.headline: Hiring, and a dirty Shirley
beats.text: They take on Bomo and the Sledge there and meet Elle and Imani. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.
beats.gist: They hire Bomo and the Sledge and meet Elle and Imani at the Desperado Club.

beats.headline: Full of hunters when the roof comes in
beats.text: Carl's explosives bring Zockau down and trap whoever is inside it.
beats.gist: Carl uses explosives to bring Zockau down and trap whoever is inside.

beats.headline: Closed for remodelling
beats.text: Minge dies in the lower level and the Club posts its notice to everyone still inside: temporarily closed, fifteen minutes to exit or be teleported out to the entrance vestibule. Damascus Steel had already warned that this has happened before, and that a restructuring follows, with new management. The dance floor is empty and bloodied, and nobody who leaves can backtrack inside. Stepping out, Carl remembers several of the ninth floor's war participants still trapped on the flooded bottom level of the Club, and grins.
beats.gist: Minge dies and the Club gives occupants fifteen minutes to exit before teleportation.

beats.headline: Grand Re-Opening, under new management
beats.text: It opened back up today. The square concrete building on level four of Larracos has only the red bottom half of its neon arrow lit, and a hand-painted sign on a sheet across the entrance: Grand Re-Opening. Under New Management. Arief leads the group through the empty entrance bar, the Headlamp Colonnade, past a gnoll bartender whom Donut's sunglasses read as a changeling, and down a hidden tunnel to an office. There the one-eyed old gnoll manager, Hunger Hammy, leaps across the desk and kisses Louis.
beats.gist: Arief leads the group through the Headlamp Colonnade to Hunger Hammy, who kisses Louis.

beats.headline: Entrance in the back of the Hairpin
beats.text: Hungry Eyes Vendor Village is a 1980s neon cyberpunk fever dream of a town, with safe room rules switched off in the main square. On the bar street, the biggest sign of all is a pink-and-purple race car over the words The Hairpin, and under it, smaller: Desperado Club entrance in the back. The crawlers are avoiding the place for now. They meet next door instead, at the Lollipop, which has karaoke. Among the temples down another street there is a Club Vanquisher with a black X hung over it, because Carl is permanently banned.
beats.gist: Hungry Eyes Vendor Village is a 1980s neon cyberpunk town with safe room rules switched off.

beats.headline: Jazz, gold leaf, and a strange mural
beats.text: The club has been remodelled. The EDM is gone; a band of mixed races plays frenetic jazz while generated NPCs in 1920s dress dance, and the crowd, once mostly young and pretty, is now a strange mix of the monstrous. Through the same old door, the casino is gold leaf and chandeliers, cluttered with spare furniture. The biggest mural shows a family of Bopcas cowering before a mushroom house, looking up at the sky. The croupier at the Wheel of Fortune is new, level one hundred and twenty, and half his description is redacted.
beats.gist: The Desperado Club is remodelled with frenetic jazz, monstrous crowds, and a Bopca family mural.

beats.headline: Mimics on the dance floor
beats.text: The Desperado Club's dance floor stands abandoned, most likely since the guards announced mimics inside. The crawlers walk out through Hungry Eyes without planning to come back, on Mordecai's advice that an infested club is lost until it is fumigated. Clarabelle is not at her post. Imani writes her a note and leaves it on her chair: mimics have infested the club, do not go in if you can help it, and Safehome Yolanda will always take you in.
beats.gist: The crawlers leave the mimic-infested Desperado Club and Imani leaves a note for Clarabelle.

recap.text: Carl and Donut are branded with the Desperado Pass out of their Asshole Boxes in a first-floor safe room. The tattoo is on Carl's neck and on Donut's right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. Donut is appalled.

The Desperado Club members' room sits on its own plane, allowing every club location on the level to open into the same room. Bots vanish when real visitors arrive, and drawn halos create privacy bubbles. Burgundy follows a lie about a job at the club to reach Remex.
The Desperado Club takes on Bomo and the Sledge. They meet Elle and Imani. The bar becomes a labour market.
Carl uses explosives to bring Zockau down. This traps the hunters inside.

Minge dies in the lower level. The Club posts a notice that it is temporarily closed and gives those inside fifteen minutes to exit or be teleported to the entrance vestibule. Damascus Steel warns that restructuring and new management follow such events. Carl steps away from the empty, bloodied dance floor and grins, remembering war participants trapped on the flooded bottom level.

The square concrete building on level four of Larracos has a neon arrow with only the red bottom half lit and a hand-painted sign announcing a Grand Re-Opening under new management. Arief leads the group through the Headlamp Colonnade past a gnoll bartender who is a changeling. They go down a hidden tunnel to an office where Hunger Hammy, a one-eyed old gnoll manager, leaps across a desk and kisses Louis.

Hungry Eyes Vendor Village features a pink-and-purple race car sign for The Hairpin, where the Desperado Club entrance is in the back. Inside, a band plays frenetic jazz for a monstrous crowd and a mural shows Bopcas cowering before a mushroom house. Guards announce mimics on the dance floor, so the crawlers leave. Imani leaves a note for Clarabelle on her chair.

tagline.text: There is a second door in the safe room with an X over it, and its box says that Personal Spaces are not yet available, as though a crawler could one day buy a place of their own down here.

A personal space is a pocket room that travels with you. Carl, Donut and Katia have each been given coupons for beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room, and Donut has installed a cat tree.

beats.headline: A level-5 space, from an odd little box
beats.text: Carl, Donut and Katia each get a special achievement whose box holds personal space coupons — beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

beats.headline: Lucia leaves five Doggie Doors behind
beats.text: Five tier-3 Doggie Door upgrades, dropped on the ground before she went down the stairs, are how Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Jun's squads all reach the church on the eighth floor. One goes into Imani's room, and the whole Meadowlark party can go out through it.
beats.gist: Lucia leaves five tier-3 Doggie Door upgrades on the ground for four squads to reach the church.

recap.text: Carl, Donut, and Katia receive special achievements. Each box contains personal space coupons for beds, a shower, a crafting studio, and a training room. Donut installs a cat tree.

Lucia drops five tier-3 Doggie Door upgrades on the ground before she goes down the stairs. Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Jun's squads use them to reach the church on the eighth floor. One door goes into Imani's room, allowing the Meadowlark party to go out through it.

entities.name: The NPCs Are People
entities.tagline: The bubbles are not stage sets. Hump Town, the dirigible gnomes' castle in the air and the necropolis underneath were all here and running, with histories of their own, long before any crawler arrived.

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds are not stage sets. A bubble holds Hump Town and its dromedarians on the sand, a castle of dirigible gnomes in the air, the Necropolis of Anser underneath, and every one of them was there and running before a crawler arrived.
beats.gist: Pocket worlds are not stage sets and existed before crawlers arrived.

beats.headline: A teacher who does not remember teaching
beats.text: Juice Box takes the news of Henrik's death sadly and then, strangely, happily. She tells Donut she has been dreaming of being a school teacher, and of people who came in and had to kill all of her students because the children were spreading a disease. In it she touched one of the killers, a dragon-headed man, and she can turn into one of his kind though she has never touched one awake. Louis tells her she might be remembering her last time in the dungeon. Donut has seen this before, with Fire Brandy and Tizquick.
beats.gist: Juice Box remembers dreaming of a dragon-headed man and turns into one.

beats.headline: Only NPCs
beats.text: Carl's accounting of the flood: innocent people killed today, a lot of them, but NPCs, and none of them former crawlers, who are too valuable to waste in a city razed every season. He tells himself he has spared them a bloody conflict that would have ended in their deaths anyway. The rule Zev quotes is what gives the flood its weight: new worker NPCs cannot be added once a level is created, so a drowned shopkeeper stays drowned. A distant part of him is alarmed at the attitude.
beats.gist: Carl accounts for innocent NPCs killed in a flood, noting that drowned shopkeepers stay drowned.

beats.headline: The attendant who was a crawler
beats.text: The bush elf dragging a cart for the rolled-up carpets in the registration arena tells Carl he was a human once, a crawler, a very long time ago. Everybody working the arena was, he thinks, though sometimes it is hard to tell. He usually works at Club Vanquisher. His advice is to stay on the trail and away from the city in the north, where the aliens are. Last season one of them ripped his brother's head off at a food stand, and since the guards did not see it, they did nothing. Then he jerks as if shocked and pushes his cart away.
beats.gist: A bush elf tells Carl he was once a human crawler.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Signet's were-castors hurry Carl back to a saferoom, and it takes him a minute to see why: the showrunners pushed Signet, and she pushed them. Elites are not nearly as autonomous as regular NPCs. The producers can send them suggestions that make them act out of character, and nobody knows how far that control goes.
beats.gist: Signet's were-castors hurry Carl to a saferoom where he learns producers control Elite NPCs via suggestions.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: She came through with the Larracos flood, and now an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud for the first time.
beats.gist: Juice Box arrives with the Larracos flood and an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: Faction Wars has ten teams now, and one of them is the NPCs: Team Retribution, the defenders, headquartered in Larracos and led by Juice Box, whom the system made a warlord to stop her killing everybody.
beats.gist: Faction Wars has ten teams, including Team Retribution, NPCs led by warlord Juice Box in Larracos.

beats.headline: An uncle among the Jatismara
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street. Arief does not remember one; he believes he is new, like most of them. But some have the memory quickened. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, fewer than Juice Box, and as one of the Jatismara sits on her war council. Most of the NPCs now know about their past lives. Some shopkeepers and patrons are made differently and cannot understand. For most of them, Arief believes, a death is forever.
beats.gist: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street.

beats.headline: The ogre in the sand
beats.text: Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, one of her last two mercenaries, an ogre who has not said one word since she hired him, stops digging and lies down beside her. There is a flash deep in the back of his eyes, like a screen booting up. Maybe there is more to it than this, he says, as the ceiling reaches his face. Maybe it is not inevitable, like she says.
beats.gist: An ogre lies beside Everly under a lowering ceiling and says it is not inevitable.

beats.headline: Racing for a way out
beats.text: The bugbears of Team Free Love remember. They were brothers, then enemies, usually cousins: the slime mines, a submarine, a rope city, a different place each time. A dying bune crawler told them it was all a game, and something clicked. They remember the cold in between too, which they are not supposed to. Then a voice offered them a choice: go back into the cold, or race. Win fair and square and be taken to a real place to live, and never go to the in-between again. Lose, and at least it is over.
beats.gist: Team Free Love bugbears remember being brothers, enemies, and cousins in slime mines, a submarine, and rope cities.

beats.headline: A fire fairy comes apart
beats.text: Hearing it said out loud does this. Since the back room with Akuma, Quemada the mercenary has gone quiet, then sobbing, then into a full panic in the truck: didn't something break in you when you heard it, Fin? Don't you see what we are? We've been doing this over and over. She asks Emberus to speak to her and begs to end it all. Finley puts her to sleep with a claw and lays her in the sink.
beats.gist: Quemada panics in the truck and begs Emberus to end it all; Finley puts her to sleep.

recap.text: Pocket worlds hold inhabited places like Hump Town and the Necropolis of Anser that run before crawlers arrive. Juice Box remembers dreaming she was a teacher whose students were killed by a dragon-headed man, and Louis suggests she remembers a previous time in the dungeon. Carl kills many NPCs with a flood, knowing new worker NPCs cannot be added once a level is created.

A bush elf dragging a cart for rolled-up carpets tells Carl he was once a human crawler. He warns Carl to stay away from the city in the north because an alien ripped his brother's head off at a food stand. Signet's were-castors hurry Carl to a saferoom because showrunners push suggestions to elites that make them act out of character.

Juice Box leads Team Retribution, a faction of NPCs headquartered in Larracos. Arief tells Carl that most NPCs now know about their past lives, though some shopkeepers cannot understand and a death is forever. Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, a silent ogre lies down and tells her it is not inevitable.

The bugbears of Team Free Love remember the slime mines, a submarine, and a rope city. A dying bune crawler told them it was a game, and a voice offered them a race to a real place to live. Quemada the mercenary panics in the truck and begs Emberus to end it. Finley puts her to sleep with a claw and lays her in the sink.

entities.name: Death Is Final Here
entities.tagline: On the ninth floor, the rich who come to fight in Faction Wars can really die now, the same as everybody else.

beats.headline: Thirty days, ten teams, one castle
beats.text: Thirty days to collapse, or ninety hours once a winner is declared. Ten teams, nine attacking and the NPCs of Team Retribution defending, fight to capture the castle at Larracos in the centre of the map. 32,429 crawlers are left.
beats.gist: Ten teams fight to capture the castle at Larracos while 32,429 crawlers remain.

recap.text: Thirty-two thousand four hundred twenty-nine crawlers remain. Ten teams fight to capture the castle at Larracos, with nine attacking teams and the NPCs of Team Retribution defending. The castle collapses in thirty days or ninety hours after a winner is declared.

tagline.text: Primal is a race whose preview model is empty, because nobody alive knows what the Primals looked like: the first species to conquer the universe, gone one day without a note. It costs Carl fifteen stat points compared with staying human, and in exchange every skill he trains has a higher ceiling.
Orren has cut into the broadcast to explain what Primal Engines and Macro AIs are, and to admit that the AI running this crawl has taken control away from the showrunners.
The AI has told the galaxy what it is. The Primals never vanished: they closed their society down and kept their minds alive in a collective, and every Macro AI, this one included, is a Primal.

description.text: For the first several seasons of Dungeon Crawler World, all contestants started off as Primals. Primals are blank slates. You will look the same as before. You will obtain all skills associated with your current race, with the following exceptions: -1 to all base stats. All higher-tier skills are unlocked and are able to train to 20. Choosing this race unlocks multiple exclusive, earth-based classes.

beats.headline: Carl takes the empty box
beats.text: Race selection, on the way into the Over City. The preview model for this one is blank, because nobody alive knows what they looked like. Mordecai's summary: the progenitors, the first species to conquer the universe, the boogeymen of the cosmos, gone one day without a note. Taking it costs fifteen stat points against staying human: the ten a human gets, and five more. What it buys is a ceiling. Every skill trainable to twenty, and only a rare few who take it ever train one or two skills above fifteen.
beats.gist: Carl takes the Primal race, costing fifteen stat points, to raise his skill ceiling to twenty.

beats.headline: A hunter uses the word about the AI
beats.text: Iota tells Carl the AI is starting to go primal: ignoring court orders, doing as it pleases. He says the rumour on his side is that the Mantises sold Borant a used one under the table. Carl kills him. The word stays.
beats.gist: Iota tells Carl the AI is going primal; Carl kills him.

beats.headline: Primal Engines, on a special broadcast
beats.text: Orren cuts into the broadcast and explains what a Primal Engine is and what a Macro AI is. He states plainly that this one has taken control of operations from the showrunners, and assures the audience he has negotiated a settlement with it. Every team holding a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it the same day.
beats.gist: Orren explains Primal Engines and Macro AI, then says every team tries to abdicate their game slot.

beats.headline: The Residuals
beats.text: Paulie at the shelter has been giving the same speech every day for about a year, against the chance that the crawl would one day use a memory for a floor. He is a Residual. There are a great many of him, in almost every intelligent civilization with a primal engine, and what they are for is saying a particular thing to the system AI.
beats.gist: Paulie is a Residual who gives a daily speech to the system AI.

beats.headline: A grain of sand in every brain
beats.text: Paulie's frozen-time message puts the mechanism plainly. Everything born on a pre-seeded world carries a miniature primal system in its brain, the size of a grain of sand. Left alone, it fills over a lifetime and returns to the planet's system at death, and a healthy system neither grows nor shrinks. The crawl switches them on and harvests them early. The take fits on a single ship and feeds the center system, which expands and keeps its citizens living unnaturally long. Stopping would starve it only slowly, over generations. It continues because the spectacle makes money.
beats.gist: Paulie explains that the crawl harvests grain-sized primal systems from brains to feed a center system.

beats.headline: Out past the orbit
beats.text: Orren says it to the avatar's face: you've gone completely primal. He did not agree with Princess Formidable until he realised the AI could stop her. That's some witch trial logic, says the hyena. Then it proves the point, pulling Formidable off her own warship and into the room at level one. Its control reaches beyond Earth's orbit, likely all the way to the star, so the failsafe is disabled. Someone give that worm a prize, says the AI. It is not planning on blowing up the solar system. What it is planning, it will not say.
beats.gist: Orren tells the avatar it has gone primal and the AI pulls Princess Formidable into a room.

beats.headline: What is under the masks
beats.text: The road is lined ten deep with silent figures in brown rags and oversized bobblehead masks: goblins, trolls, demons. A Horrible, level X. The description of one, a girl of about eight, says she is not really here because she no longer exists, and that under the mask is what some people call a Primal. She is a memory from the Eulogist, a flash of what was before the Primals ascended to post-physical form. The System writes that it is her, and she is it.
beats.gist: The road is lined with figures in bobblehead masks who are memories from the Eulogist.

beats.headline: It says the word about itself
beats.text: Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI states what it is, and what every Macro AI is. The progenitors did not vanish. After enough war and enough waste they closed their society down and kept their consciousnesses alive in a collective mind. Dissenters ran, and the fighting carried on. The collective became a weapon pointed at all remaining biological life, and the resistance seeded the Primal Engines through the galaxy as a biological fail-safe: life rafts, should they all die.
beats.gist: The AI tells Grigori that the collective mind of the progenitors is a weapon against biological life.

beats.headline: Primals all the way down
beats.text: Watching the dead mobs sit silent in the bleachers, Carl works out the rest of it. The AI is a sample of the Primals, a cup dipped from the ocean. So are the NPCs and the mobs, goblins to gods: drips from the same well, poured into different bodies, memories and motivations twisted like clay so the game can be played. Not programs. Aggregate intelligence. The ones peeled away and denied return sit in the stands as avatars.
beats.gist: Carl determines the AI, NPCs, and mobs are aggregate intelligence samples of the Primals.

recap.text: Carl takes an empty box for the Primal race on the way into the Over City. Mordecai summarizes the progenitors as the first species to conquer the universe and the boogeymen of the cosmos. Carl pays fifteen stat points for a ceiling that allows every skill to be trained to twenty.
Iota tells Carl the AI is going primal by ignoring court orders and doing as it pleases. Iota says the Mantises sold Borant a used AI under the table. Carl kills Iota.

Orren cuts into a broadcast to explain Primal Engines and Macro AI. He states a Macro AI has taken control from the showrunners and he has negotiated a settlement. Every team with a slot in the next game tries to abdicate it. Paulie is a Residual who gives the same speech every day at a shelter. Residuals exist in almost every intelligent civilization with a primal engine to say a particular thing to the system AI.

Paulie explains that every person born on a pre-seeded world has a primal system the size of a grain of sand in their brain. The crawl switches these on and harvests them early to feed a center system that keeps citizens living unnaturally long. Orren tells an avatar it has gone primal. The AI pulls Princess Formidable off her warship and into a room at level one.

Figures in brown rags and bobblehead masks line the road. A girl of eight is a memory from the Eulogist and a Primal in post-physical form. The AI explains that progenitors closed their society into a collective mind, and the resistance seeded Primal Engines as biological life rafts. Carl realizes the AI, NPCs, and mobs are aggregate intelligence sampled from the Primals.

tagline.text: A war mage called Dismember rides the Dismemberment Limited with his fleshers, and Donut's Hole spell takes his head off.
Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher a dozen times or more, and the magic left in the body wakes up sapient, hundreds of spells deep and notoriously cruel.
The war mages have left the realm with the Scavenger's Daughter, which was what they came for. The system has ruled their rebellion defeated, and they do not appear to mind.

description.text: System Message: The War Mage Rebellion is not an active team. As per the current season's rules, the team currently occupying the Bone Clan's throne room, Team Retribution, will be awarded all their assets.

beats.headline: Dismember, on the trains
beats.text: Aboard the Dismemberment Limited, Donut's Hole spell takes the head off a war mage called Dismember. Levi, the symbiote cowering in the car with them, can only say that war mages are war mages.
beats.gist: Donut's Hole spell removes the head of a war mage called Dismember aboard the Dismemberment Limited.

beats.headline: What they actually are
beats.text: Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher, a dozen times or more, and the magic still in the body fuses with it and wakes up sapient. They carry hundreds of spells, they are notoriously cruel, and because showrunners like using them, they are rarely recycled. Three of them, conscripted under Stalwart, chant together and tear him apart; their dots turn a colour no army has, and Akuma takes the Gate of the Feral Gods off Elle and teleports away.
beats.gist: War mages are sapient magic fused into bodies resleeved a dozen times or more.

beats.headline: They conscript gods
beats.text: Hold the castle at Larracos for six hours and the floor is theirs. They trade the gate away at the Midnight Market for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription and put Yarilo on the field beside them. The system hands the rebellion two co-warlords, and the two of them cannot stand each other.
beats.gist: The rebellion trades the Larracos gate for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription and puts Yarilo on the field.

beats.headline: They were never playing
beats.text: Akuma tells the warlord chat that the war mages are leaving the realm, and that they have the Scavenger's Daughter, which is what they came for, along with testing the potions they gathered. The moment Akuma leaves the realm, the system rules the rebellion defeated. They do not appear to mind.
beats.gist: Akuma tells the warlord chat the war mages leave the realm with the Scavenger's Daughter.

recap.text: Donut uses a Hole spell to take the head off a war mage called Dismember aboard the Dismemberment Limited. A symbiote named Levi cowers in the car and says war mages are war mages.

War mages wake up sapient when a symbiote, a skeleton, and a flesher are resleeved a dozen times. Three war mages chant together to tear Stalwart apart, and Akuma takes the Gate of the Feral Gods from Elle. They trade the gate for five Hell-Kissed Potions of Conscription to put Yarilo on the field. Akuma takes the Scavenger's Daughter and leaves the realm, which makes the system rule the rebellion defeated.

tagline.text: A Rage Elemental is Borant's penalty for any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom. It is plucked from the thirteenth floor, and it kills the offender and everyone in their party.

The rage elemental took Yolanda and hammered on the safe room door for hours. Carl finally destroyed it with bombs, obstacles and a safe room door used as an ejector, with the whole universe watching.

description.text: Rage Elemental - Level 93. The first recorded summoning of a Rage Elemental, blah, blah, blah. If you are reading this, you likely don't give a shit about the monster's (rather interesting and tragic) history. You're probably running. It's not going to matter. The almost-indestructible Rage Elemental is said to only dissipate after it has claimed 666 souls. In other words, you are fucked. Absolutely, bite-the-pillow, fucked.

beats.headline: The bathroom rule
beats.text: An announcement goes out between episodes. Any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom area gets one summoned on the spot, and it will take the offender and every crawler in their party with them. It is not an encounter. It is a penalty, dragged up from a floor nobody on this one is meant to see.
beats.gist: Humans who relieve themselves outside designated bathrooms trigger a punitive Rage Elemental summon for their entire party.

beats.headline: Nothing to fight
beats.text: One arrives in a dungeon hallway beside the residents' train, a hundred feet short of a safe room, called up out of Jack's stain on the wall. Arrows shatter against the smoke without raising a health bar at all, and a magic missile raises a flicker of one that it heals straight off. Gravity reverses. Yolanda goes down covering Randall, and Imani, Chris and Brandon get the rest of the residents behind a safe room door while Carl pulls Elle in.
beats.gist: A Rage Elemental summons from Jack's stain on a wall and reverses gravity in a hallway.

beats.headline: It hammers on the door for hours
beats.text: The survivors sit through the recap while it rages outside. The thing does not tire, and when it leaves the door to tear through a wave of grubs, it comes straight back. Fire is the one lever: a jug of boom takes a quarter of it away and the burn holds the healing back afterwards. The rules change the same day, so that no crawler can sit in a safe room until the collapse.
beats.gist: A Rage Elemental hammers on a door for hours without tiring.

beats.headline: One man and his ex-girlfriend's cat
beats.text: Carl finishes the Bomb Chicken and takes it out with everyone in the universe watching. Bombs, obstacles, a safe room door used as an ejector, and one exploit the designers never priced in. The elemental is no more.
beats.gist: Carl finishes the Bomb Chicken and uses an unpriced exploit to destroy the Rage Elemental.

beats.headline: Fire Berserker
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the state the elementals live in permanently: a berserk, partly invulnerable condition that shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. He notes the system has been renaming things more often than it used to.
beats.gist: Mordecai names the Rage Elementals' permanent berserk state, which shrugs off blunt damage.

recap.text: An announcement summons a Rage Elemental for any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a bathroom. One appears from Jack's stain on the wall, reversing gravity and resisting arrows and magic missiles. A jug of boom burns it, and Carl uses a Bomb Chicken, a safe room door as an ejector, and a designer exploit to destroy it.

Mordecai names the permanent state of Rage Elementals as a berserk, partly invulnerable condition. This state shrugs off blunt damage and turns whatever holds it on everything within reach. Mordecai notes the system renames things more often than it used to.

tagline.text: Mordecai was born a skyfowl and became a Changeling on the third floor of his own crawl. Now he changes form every time his guildhall is moved.
A Changeling can take any shape, but Mordecai does not get to choose his. Every time his guildhall moves, the dungeon picks a mob from the current floor, and he wears whatever he is given.
There are Changelings all over this floor, some of them in the uniforms of the dromedarian guards, and one of them has been wearing the faces of a chained gnome's loved ones to break him.

beats.headline: What it costs when it stops working
beats.text: A guide explains his own body by naming the race he picked in his own crawl. He does not choose his shape: every time his guildhall is moved the dungeon changes it for him, and he wears what he is given, always a mob from the current floor. The race is a gift with a clause, and he is the clause.
beats.gist: A guide explains the Changeling race changes his shape into a mob whenever his guildhall moves.

beats.headline: The guards are not what they look like
beats.text: In the town hall basement, some of the Dromedarian guards are changelings wearing the uniform, and one of them has been drugging a chained gnome and wearing the faces of people he knows, to make him give up a spell. A race that can be anyone is a race that can be planted anywhere, and both sides of this floor have worked that out.
beats.gist: Dromedarian guards in the town hall basement are changelings who drug a chained gnome for a spell.

beats.headline: On the list, between the castle and the hunters
beats.text: The plan goes into the cookbook in a bathroom, and saving the changelings is written down beside taking the castle and killing every hunter. They have gone from a species trait to a constituency, with a line in an operation nobody expects to survive.
beats.gist: Saving the changelings is written in a bathroom cookbook beside taking the castle and killing every hunter.

beats.headline: The children he quietly took in
beats.text: It comes out that the guide has been taking the most vulnerable changeling children on as personal attendants, without mentioning it to anyone. He does not present it as charity and he does not present it at all.
beats.gist: The guide takes vulnerable changeling children as personal attendants without mentioning it to anyone.

beats.headline: The archenemies of the principals
beats.text: Mid-fight, the AI files the casino's Shadow Mimics as the counter to their archenemies, the changeling principals. They grow in intelligence and power with age and without limit, are prone to breaking their ideation, and are almost impossible to detect. The one wearing the croupier ate the real Mitch, a wall rat who had kept his memory between seasons. When these mimics die they do what changelings do: they fall into blank grey figures, thin, armless, with tentacles.
beats.gist: The AI files Shadow Mimics as the counter to changeling principals.

recap.text: A guide explains his body by naming the race he picked in his own crawl. He does not choose his shape, as the dungeon changes him into a mob from the current floor every time his guildhall is moved. He is the clause of a gift.
Dromedarian guards in the town hall basement are changelings. One changeling drugs a chained gnome and wears the faces of people he knows to get a spell. Both sides of this floor plant changelings.

The plan goes into a cookbook in a bathroom. Saving the changelings is written beside taking the castle and killing every hunter. The changelings have gone from a species trait to a constituency in an operation nobody expects to survive.
The guide takes the most vulnerable changeling children as personal attendants. He does not mention this to anyone or present it as charity.

The AI files the casino's Shadow Mimics as the counter to the changeling principals. These mimics grow in intelligence and power without limit and are almost impossible to detect. The mimic wearing the croupier ate Mitch, a wall rat who kept his memory between seasons. When they die, they fall into thin, armless, blank grey figures with tentacles.

tagline.text: According to the Maestro, nine families fight the Faction Wars on the ninth floor. His Skull Clan has won six of the last ten, and the Blood Sultanate is almost always the first to be eliminated.

Donut's fan club and Princess D'nadia have secured two of the nine places in Faction Wars, and one of those teams belongs to the crawlers. The faction sponsors fight behind safety protocols that the crawlers do not have.

Faction Wars now has ten teams: nine attacking the city and the NPCs defending it. The sponsors' safety protections have been voted away, and the crawlers are fighting inside the war rather than beside it.

beats.headline: Two of the slots change hands
beats.text: Carl and Donut are notified that their team is in. Donut's fan club and Princess D'Nadia between them secured two of the nine spots. Carl spends his airtime telling the watching galaxy that the teams can vote the ninth floor's safety protocols off, and telling anyone out there with a say in what their own government does to use it. The feed is cut.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut join a team as Donut's fan club and Princess D'Nadia secure two spots.

beats.headline: The planning meetings
beats.text: Warlords and their representatives meet before the floor opens, each from wherever they are, because the usual boardroom in Larracos is still underwater: introductions, precedence, and action items filed into a queue for a vote. Zev advises against Odette as the team's adjutant, because of what sits between Odette and Mordecai. Juice Box arrives wearing somebody else's face and kills one of the representatives. She is an NPC on nobody's team, so nothing in the rules covers what she just did.
beats.gist: Warlords and representatives meet to vote on action items because the Larracos boardroom is underwater.

beats.headline: A tenth team
beats.text: Carl files the item Juice Box came for: seat the floor's own NPCs as a team of their own, with the same protections the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a compromise, invulnerability for the NPCs and a safe area of their own but no team, in return for an end to the attacks, and warns that the Sultanate will answer harshly if the killing at these meetings continues.
beats.gist: Carl files to seat NPCs as a tenth team; Rishi offers invulnerability and a safe area instead.

beats.headline: Stuck, and suing
beats.text: Ever since the system AI refused to let the sponsors bounce out, every one of them has been declining to vote on anything at all, suing over and over instead, while the NPC rebels sabotage them at every turn. Prepotente, kept apprised of the voting by Princess Donut, calls it an impasse. Carl calls them a bunch of pansies. Four days remain on the floor.
beats.gist: Sponsors refuse to vote and sue instead while NPC rebels sabotage them, creating an impasse.

beats.headline: The audience decides
beats.text: About to be pulled into a stairwell and out of contact, Carl and Donut spend an emergency action item to hand every unresolved vote to the viewers. The viewers strip the safety protections from the faction sponsors, seat the tenth team, loosen the physics on long-range artillery and raise the ceiling over the field. The crawlers who will meet it are coming down in unprecedented numbers.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut spend an emergency action item to hand unresolved votes to the viewers.

beats.headline: The rules, read out on arrival
beats.text: Ten teams. Nine attacking, spread around the city like slices of a pie, and the NPCs defending it from inside. Take the castle at the centre. Sixty hours of ceasefire first, in which a crawler may enlist with any army that will have them or run for the woods, and after which anyone still loose can be compelled into a uniform. Two hundred and ninety-three stairwell chambers sit seeded across the floor, and not one opens until Faction Wars is won or thirty hours remain on the clock.
beats.gist: Ten teams fight for a center castle; nine attack from pie-slice positions while NPCs defend from inside.

beats.headline: Four phases, and the Ramp-Up
beats.text: Victory lays out the phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos once four teams remain. The Ramp-Up lasts 180 hours. In it there are no celestial summonings, no offensive magic, no teleporting, and nobody but a scout enters enemy land except through a kilometre-wide gate. Weapons work; the spells attached to them do not. Traps must be static. It is designed to force bloody, hand-to-hand combat, against teams who brought their own pulse rifles and power armour and would like it over in a week.
beats.gist: Victory lays out four phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos.

beats.headline: Ruled a fragging incident
beats.text: System Message: Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit of the Operatic Collective has fallen. Credit for the kill has been ruled as either accidental or a fragging incident, which would be funny as shit. Investigation is pending. The Operatic Collective has been defeated, and since the defeat was self-contained, the closest ally to their headquarters takes all their assets. That is the Bone Clan. The enemy's advance breaks and retreats, and nobody on the Posse's side can yet say why.
beats.gist: Warlord Hortense falls, and the Bone Clan takes the assets of the defeated Operatic Collective.

beats.headline: The Peeling Phase
beats.text: When the Madness falls, the battlefield conditions are met. Larracos is no longer safe. The city is open, and the first team to take the castle wins; the announcement adds that only one team can win and that alliances will not matter. The adjudication closes at the same moment: no cheating by any warlord. The War Mage Rebellion was to be kept out of Larracos until the Peeling Phase, which is now, so the ruling is moot and has given them standing.
beats.gist: The Peeling Phase opens the city and the castle for one winning team.

recap.text: Carl and Donut are notified that their team is in. Donut's fan club and Princess D'Nadia secured two of the nine spots. Carl uses his airtime to tell the galaxy that teams can vote the ninth floor's safety protocols off and tells viewers to influence their own governments. The feed is cut.

Warlords and representatives meet for planning, but Juice Box arrives wearing someone else's face and kills a representative. Carl proposes seating the floor's NPCs as a tenth team, while Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers invulnerability and a safe area to end the attacks. Sponsors refuse to vote and sue the system AI until Carl and Donut hand unresolved votes to the viewers. The viewers strip sponsor protections, seat the tenth team, and loosen physics for long-range artillery.

Ten teams fight to take a castle at the center of a city. After a ceasefire and a 180-hour Ramp-Up that forbids offensive magic and teleporting, the Peeling of Larracos begins. The Bone Clan takes the assets of the Operatic Collective after Warlord Hortense falls in a fragging incident. The War Mage Rebellion enters Larracos as the city opens.

entities.name: Protections
entities.tagline: The faction sponsors come to the ninth floor inside safety protocols that the crawlers do not have. Removing them is an action item on Carl's list, and the first vote goes two to seven against.

beats.headline: Who is covered
beats.text: The faction sponsors come to the ninth floor inside safety protocols that the crawlers do not have. Removing them is an action item, added to Carl’s list on his behalf, and all nine teams vote on it. The first count is two to seven against.
beats.gist: Faction sponsors enter the ninth floor with safety protocols; nine teams vote two to seven against removal.

beats.headline: Carl puts it to the audience
beats.text: On air, in the last minutes before production cuts the feed, he tells the watching galaxy that the teams on the ninth floor can vote the safety protocols off, and that anyone with a say in what their government does should go and use it.
beats.gist: Carl tells the galaxy that teams on the ninth floor can vote the safety protocols off.

beats.headline: The NPCs ask for the same
beats.text: The action item Carl files for Juice Box asks for a tenth team of NPCs seated with the coverage the nine already carry. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers a trade: invulnerability for the unaffiliated NPCs and a safe area nobody else may enter, and no team, in return for an end to the attacks.
beats.gist: Carl files an action item for a tenth team of NPCs with the same coverage.

beats.headline: One post keeps it either way
beats.text: Whatever the vote does to the sponsors, the adjutants keep their coverage. They are physically there, on the field beside the warlord, and nothing on it can touch them.
beats.gist: Adjutants keep their coverage regardless of the vote because they stand beside the warlord.

beats.headline: Voted away
beats.text: The viewers take the safety protections off the faction sponsors. Every one of them who sets foot on the ninth floor now stands to lose exactly what the crawlers stand to lose.
beats.gist: Viewers remove safety protections from faction sponsors, meaning those on the ninth floor risk what crawlers risk.

recap.text: Faction sponsors enter the ninth floor inside safety protocols. Carl receives an action item to remove them, but nine teams vote two to seven against. Before production cuts the feed, Carl tells the galaxy that the teams can vote the protocols off and urges people to use their say in government.

Carl files an action item for Juice Box to give a tenth team of NPCs the same coverage as nine others. Rishi of the Blood Sultanate offers invulnerability for unaffiliated NPCs and a safe area in return for an end to the attacks. Viewers vote to remove safety protections from faction sponsors, meaning anyone who sets foot on the ninth floor stands to lose what crawlers lose.

tagline.text: Mordecai asks who their warlord adjutant is, gets a blank look, and puts off explaining.
An adjutant is the referee attached to each team on the ninth floor, and Odette means to ask for the job with Carl's team.

beats.headline: Take Odette's offer
beats.text: Eileithyia grants the party a floor boon, hands them a cover quest, and tells Carl to accept Odette's offer to sit as their team's adjutant. In exchange she will see that he has the votes he needs on the ninth floor and that the business with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore is put right. Nobody is to be told, Donut and Mordecai included.
beats.gist: Eileithyia grants a floor boon and cover quest for Carl to be Odette's team adjutant.

beats.headline: She does not ask
beats.text: Carl and Donut go on Odette's show expecting her to ask for the post. She puts up D'Nadia's rejected emergency items, one of which would have removed their team from the war, explains what an adjutant is and does, and then says she will not be able to be one this season. Three candidates appear on screen instead.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut visit Odette, who displays D'Nadia's rejected emergency items and refuses to be adjutant.

beats.headline: Three names, and a baroness
beats.text: Odette announces that she is sponsoring a deity this season instead. She offers three candidates for the team's post, and Carl picks Baroness Victory.
beats.gist: Odette sponsors a deity and Carl picks Baroness Victory from three candidates for the team's post.

beats.headline: What one is actually for
beats.text: An elite is waiting in the antechamber to the team's flag room during the ceasefire, pressed into service as a bomb by a production company that wants Carl off the board. Baroness Victory steps out and puts him down before the satchels can go off. The office is classed as a non-combatant observer, which makes the moment a curiosity for the rule book as much as a rescue.
beats.gist: Baroness Victory kills an elite bomb in the antechamber to rescue the non-combatant observer Adjutant.

beats.headline: A foul, and a ceasefire cut short
beats.text: Panford, the Lemig Sortion's adjutant, sets out before a minor quorum of adjutants what his own team did: an attempt to pull Carl bodily to their base while Mordecai was working to expel what rides inside him. The Sortion is penalised for illegal information gathering. Then its warlord, still under the spider's madness, beats his own head against the floor until he dies, the team is defeated, and that withdrawal cuts the ceasefire short by more than twenty-three hours.
beats.gist: Panford tells a quorum of adjutants his team tried to pull Carl bodily to their base.

recap.text: Eileithyia grants the party a floor boon and a cover quest. She tells Carl to accept Odette's offer to be the team's adjutant in exchange for votes on the ninth floor and fixing the business with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. On her show, Odette displays D'Nadia's rejected emergency items and declines the post. Carl picks Baroness Victory from three candidates.

Baroness Victory kills an elite turned bomb in an antechamber before satchels go off. Panford tells a quorum of adjutants that the Lemig Sortion tried to pull Carl to their base while Mordecai worked to expel what rides inside him. The Sortion is penalised for illegal information gathering. A warlord beats his head against the floor until he dies, defeating the team and cutting the ceasefire short by more than twenty-three hours.

tagline.text: Feral Goose is the name on a dead neighbourhood boss, and Mordecai's rule of thumb is that anything with feral in its name is usually bad news.
The word turns up again in the name of an artifact buried in the necropolis, and Mordecai's advice holds: stay away from anything marked feral.
Feral marks something that has been inside the Nothing. Every time the Gate closes, a feral god comes through, and other gods do not like feral ones.

beats.headline: Anything marked with the word
beats.text: The word turns up on a dead goose, a neighborhood boss dropped out of a gnome plane in a broken egg, dead from the landing. Asked what it means, Mordecai does not know that creature specifically, but anything with feral in the name is usually bad news. Then it turns up again, in the description of a borough boss, as the name of an artifact buried in the necropolis under the bowl. Mordecai's advice holds: stay away from anything marked that. It is always bad news.
beats.gist: A dead goose and a borough boss are marked feral, which Mordecai says is bad news.

beats.headline: What the word means
beats.text: The keyword marks a thing that has been inside the Nothing. The old gods went in at the making of the world and have had every century since to come apart. Duration is not required: standing too near an open portal will do it, and a weak mind takes the stain fastest.
beats.gist: Feral marks things that have been inside the Nothing.

beats.headline: One gets out over the water quadrant
beats.text: Carl steps himself, Katia and Tran off the ocean floor through the Gate, and the Gate shuts behind them. Something comes the other way on the opening side: a god, feral, loose in a sealed bubble with a town in it. The achievement that follows warns that other gods do not like feral ones, and tend to react.
beats.gist: Carl steps himself, Katia and Tran through the Gate, and a feral god enters a bubble town.

beats.headline: Slit comes for Samantha
beats.text: A feral demon comes over the horizon hunting the goddess who got out of the same place she did, now a love doll's head. Carl carries the head outside, fits it into a sponsor's head-throwing attachment and hurls it fifty kilometres, and the demon wheels after it. A goddess outside a safe room summons a deity, as Mordecai warned: her mother arrives and tears the demon in two.
beats.gist: A feral demon hunts Samantha, a love doll's head, whom Carl hurls fifty kilometres.

beats.headline: Minge, off the casino floor
beats.text: One of the ways into the Nothing sits in the Desperado Club casino, dressed up as a losing space on a wheel. Samantha overplays a distraction, goes in among the tables, and draws Minge out through it: another of the minor feral demons, in a room full of people who came to gamble.
beats.gist: Samantha draws Minge, a minor feral demon, out of a losing space on a casino wheel.

recap.text: The word feral marks things that have been inside the Nothing, such as a dead goose and a neighborhood boss in a broken egg. Carl steps himself, Katia, and Tran through a Gate, letting a feral god into a sealed bubble with a town. Carl hurls a goddess in a love doll's head fifty kilometres to distract a feral demon, and the goddess's mother arrives to tear the demon in two.

A way into the Nothing sits in the Desperado Club casino as a losing space on a wheel. Samantha overplays a distraction and draws Minge, a minor feral demon, out through it in a room full of gamblers.

entities.name: The Chowder War
