entities.tagline: Every season, the land crabs leave their forests to spawn in the ocean, and the monk seals, who hold those waters sacred, consider it a sacrilege most foul. The System has made it a quest, and the crawlers are getting involved whether they like it or not.

description.text: New Quest. The Chowder War. Oh, you're getting involved whether you like it or not. The Monk Seals. The Red Maníseros Land Crabs. War is brewing, as it often does in these parts. Every season, the land crabs emerge from their forests to attend their sex parties in the oceans surrounding these lands. The Monk Seals hold the ocean sacred, and the very act of spilling so much crab chowder into their holy waters is considered a sacrilege most foul... Choose a side. Put an end to this conflict, one way or another. Reward: You will receive a Platinum Quest Box.

beats.headline: Out hunting monk seals, home with a war
beats.text: The party goes looking for monk seals to fill its squad slots and picks up the quest instead. Two populations, one coastline, one annual event that neither side can negotiate around, and a platinum box waiting for whoever settles it.
beats.gist: The party hunts monk seals to fill squad slots and picks up a quest for a platinum box.

beats.headline: The crabs go early and go south
beats.text: The migration opens as a sneak attack. Rather than spread along the coast the crabs mass where the seals are thinnest and run for the water together. Carl and Donut go down to flag one of them.
beats.gist: Crabs mass where seals are thinnest and run for the water; Carl and Donut flag one.

beats.headline: Sister Ines takes the other side
beats.text: She reaches an agreement with the Monk Seal Abbot and warns him what the crabs are doing. That turns a slaughter into a battle, and puts two crawlers at opposite ends of the same quest.
beats.gist: Sister Ines warns the Monk Seal Abbot about the crabs, turning a slaughter into a battle.

beats.headline: Failed, and something worse announced
beats.text: Samantha scouts ahead and finds Sister Ines on a giant snake, with zombie pups crawling over it, and living seals singing and living crabs dancing around it. The quest fails. Hell Comes to Crawler Town is announced in its place, and so much death reaches the underworld that Sheol overflows and starts evicting its demons upward into the weakened and the freshly dead.
beats.gist: Samantha finds Sister Ines on a giant snake with zombie pups, singing seals, and dancing crabs.

beats.headline: The same flavour of chowder
beats.text: The Missing Piece quest updates mid-battle: the eviction that brought Amayon here is his undoing: now in his true form, he lacks the power to cast his spell home, and the dying world has too few souls left to trigger it. The fix it hints at is to refill the world with the same type of souls that set the whole thing off. The same flavour of chowder, it says. The announcers had it that the eviction began because the AI counted crab sperm as a mob, so the answer is a crab, a beach full of corpses, and the eggs still out in the water.
beats.gist: The Missing Piece quest updates; Amayon lacks the power to cast his spell home.

recap.text: The party hunts monk seals and takes a quest to settle a conflict between two populations for a platinum box. Carl and Donut flag crabs during a sneak attack, while Sister Ines warns the Monk Seal Abbot. Samantha finds Sister Ines on a giant snake with zombie pups, and the quest fails. Hell Comes to Crawler Town begins as Sheol evicts demons into the dead. The Missing Piece quest updates to refill the world with crab souls.

entities.name: The Recital
entities.tagline: The Recital is a quest that arrived on the day Donut renamed the town Point Mongo. Something is driving the dinosaurs at its fences, and the crawlers must find out what they want, or exterminate them.

description.text: New Quest! The Recital. Dinosaur attacks are becoming more and more of a problem in the large settlement of Point Mongo. It started small. A chicken here. An Ursine there. People didn't care so much at first since they were mostly picking off the annoying people. But the attacks are getting worse. The dinosaurs probing the town's defenses are getting bigger... Exterminate the threat. Or, find out what they want, and then give it to them. I'll leave it up to you. Reward: You will receive a Gold Quest Box! You will also receive a free town upgrade!

beats.headline: A town, newly named, with a dinosaur problem
beats.text: Donut renames the settlement Point Mongo and the quest arrives on the same day. Mongo takes her off into the jungle on his back and finds the pack: all female, all mongoliensis, headed by one called Kiwi. When Carl carries Donut back to town, Mongo stays behind.
beats.gist: Donut renames the settlement Point Mongo and a quest arrives.

beats.headline: A name for the thing at the fences
beats.text: Samantha's reconnaissance across the water finds the ursines on the far shore torn apart, and the quest updates with the culprit: Big Tina, the dinosaur behind the raids on Point Mongo.
beats.gist: Samantha finds torn apart ursines across the water, and the quest names Big Tina as the culprit.

beats.headline: Kill her or give her what she wants
beats.text: Quest Update. Big Tina is out of control, killing every ursine she can find, and if she is not dealt with soon the High Elves may field their army, which nobody wants. Kill her or give her what she wants. Carl assumes that means killing all the ursine. Princess Donut, who has seen Footloose, says it is obvious: she wants to dance, so they have to finish the recital. A second update arrives once the minions show themselves. Surprise, it says. You don't know the half of it.
beats.gist: Big Tina kills every ursine, so Carl and Donut must kill her or finish the recital.

beats.headline: The wand casts the Recital
beats.text: From the stage, Donut reads the recharge scroll, and Big Tina's inert wand glows in her claw. It shoots sparkles, and it also casts a spell called The Recital: everyone already staring at the dinosaur is suddenly happy to be there, as if this were something they had been looking forward to. Tina hops, shaking the stage, and twirls. The cretins raise a painted mainsail behind her, and when it drops there are thirty velociraptors plus Mongo and Kiwi in homemade sea-creature costumes.
beats.gist: Donut reads a recharge scroll, making Big Tina's inert wand shoot sparkles and cast The Recital.

beats.headline: It was never about the town
beats.text: Donut spends an I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi and turns her back into an Ursine, and Tina recognises her mother. What the child wanted was never the recital: it was the mother the transmutation had turned into a dinosaur, who had been at her side the whole time. The quest closes on that.
beats.gist: Donut uses an I Take It All Back potion to turn Kiwi back into an Ursine.

recap.text: Donut renames a settlement Point Mongo. Samantha finds ursines torn apart on a far shore by a dinosaur called Big Tina. Donut decides Big Tina wants to dance, so they finish a recital. Donut uses an I Take It All Back potion on Kiwi, turning her back into an ursine mother. Big Tina recognizes her mother, and the quest closes.

entities.name: CrawlCon
entities.tagline: CrawlCon is the galaxy's fan convention, held once every other season, with thousands attending in person and billions virtually. Carl's fans have voted him onto the roster, and no active crawler has been on it in more than a century.

description.text: Thanks to your fans, you've been added to the CrawlCon roster! You will attend three events! Your presence at the con will be virtual. Please see your outreach associate for details on your schedule.

beats.headline: What it is
beats.text: Panels, autograph tables, special guests, crawlers both new and old and a children's art contest, held once every other season for thousands in person and billions watching virtually. No active crawler has been on the roster in more than a century.
beats.gist: CrawlCon is a fan convention with panels, autograph tables, and a children's art contest.

beats.headline: Carl gets a booth
beats.text: Word reaches him on the sixth floor: his fans have voted him onto the roster, and attendance is not a request.
beats.gist: Fans vote Carl onto the CrawlCon roster, and attendance is not a request.

beats.headline: Judging children's drawings
beats.text: The first event is a juvenile quickdraw contest, scored out of thirty. Between rounds he learns who is moderating his panel: the mother of a hunter he put down on this floor.
beats.gist: Carl judges a juvenile quickdraw contest and learns his panel moderator is a hunter's mother.

beats.headline: The panel goes the way it was booked to go
beats.text: Dosed by his own guards into losing his inhibitions, Carl picks a fight with the moderator on stage and asks the room for the best way to get to her surviving daughter. She smashes the table and walks out. A hooded woman at the back stops her cutting him off first, then reveals herself as one of his sponsors and leaves.
beats.gist: Carl picks a fight with the moderator and asks how to find her surviving daughter.

beats.headline: Autographs, and a new sponsor
beats.text: Carl and the Popov brothers sign for a queue of fans, a good many of them dressed as him in heart-print boxers and no shoes. His replacement sponsor is announced live at the table: the Plenty.
beats.gist: Carl and the Popov brothers sign for fans in heart-print boxers while the Plenty becomes Carl's sponsor.

recap.text: CrawlCon hosts panels and a children's art contest for billions of virtual viewers. Carl is voted onto the roster and must attend. He judges a juvenile quickdraw contest and fights a moderator who is the mother of a hunter he killed. Carl and the Popov brothers sign for fans in heart-print boxers and no shoes. The Plenty is announced as his new sponsor.

tagline.text: The cookbook's twenty-second edition mentions a formal way of attaching separate parties to one another, switched on from the sixth floor, if it still exists.

The guild system is live. A charter costs upward of half a million gold, and a level-one guild joins five parties through a shared common area, with upgrades and experience that can be shared for a fee.

beats.headline: Announced after the recap
beats.text: The announcement after the recap carries the news that the guild system is going live. Crawlers can build alliances larger than a party without having to sit inside one together.
beats.gist: An announcement after the recap says the guild system is live, allowing alliances larger than a party.

beats.headline: What a charter costs
beats.text: A guild charter runs upward of five hundred thousand gold from a bopca protector. A level-one guild holds five parties or individuals, provided each has one member with a personal space of their own, and each of those spaces opens onto a shared common area. Private and party rooms stay shut. Environmental upgrades can be licensed across the membership for a small fee, and shared experience can be bought outright.
beats.gist: A guild charter costs five hundred thousand gold from a bopca protector.

beats.headline: Katia has it worked out
beats.text: Over chat, while Carl hands out weapons to the town guards, she lays out how it would work: whoever starts it leads it, neither Carl nor Donut wants the job, and Imani might if they ask. They would have to pool money to share the upgrades.
beats.gist: Katia explains that the person who starts a guild leads it and members pool money for upgrades.

beats.headline: Safehome Yolanda
beats.text: The party joins an existing guild on the same day Katia finally walks out of the party. She does not go far. The charter is what keeps her within reach of people she is no longer travelling with.
beats.gist: The party joins a guild the day Katia leaves, but the charter keeps her within reach.

beats.headline: A hundred guilds, and a party
beats.text: The daily announcement counts just over 66,000 crawlers, exactly 100 guilds combining almost 1,500 parties, and over 90% of crawlers partied with somebody. For a non-stigmergic species, says the System, you do love your societal structures, and it makes you easy targets. Hunters are hiding in Zockau, and if that goes on, things may change. The seventh floor has been completely redesigned. The top 50 will be invited to a party at the Butcher's Masquerade, attendance mandatory, each with a plus one.
beats.gist: The daily announcement counts 66,000 crawlers, 100 guilds, 1,500 parties, and mandatory attendance at the Butcher's Masquerade.

recap.text: An announcement states the guild system is live, allowing alliances larger than a party. A guild charter costs over five hundred thousand gold from a bopca protector. Katia suggests Imani lead a guild so they can pool money for upgrades. Katia leaves the party but stays nearby via a charter. The System counts 100 guilds and warns that hunters hide in Zockau.

tagline.text: Vengeance of the Daughter is a Syndicate drama shot inside the dungeon, with a circus, a half-naiad who would be tsarina if she were full-blooded, and a guest-star slot for Carl.
The grief in Vengeance of the Daughter is real, but the schedule is not. Someone outside the floor decides when Signet mourns, and counts how many are watching.
The Dream has bought Vengeance of the Daughter, and it means to collect on the third season that Carl's contract guarantees.

beats.headline: The programme has a name
beats.text: Carl has a hunch that Signet's storyline is a programme of its own. Mordecai's old friend Eklund, a game guide in the nearby town, supplies the name: Vengeance of the Daughter. Its producer is not yet taking Zev's calls. Mordecai's view of such things stands: a team of writers, very protective of their show, and an elite with thick plot armour at the centre of it.
beats.gist: Eklund tells Carl the programme is Vengeance of the Daughter.

beats.headline: Carl signs on
beats.text: He poisons Grimaldi's vine with his own blood and offers the producers a deal: he will appear on the programme when it moves to the sixth floor, or he heals the vine and their big night is a dud. They take it, and he heals the vine anyway. Then he reads a Wisp Armor spellbook for cover against mind control, accepts a cone of parasitic worms from Apollon the Mighty so he can speak inside Grimaldi's head, and talks him into lifting Signet's banishment.
beats.gist: Carl poisons Grimaldi's vine with blood to force a deal with the producers.

beats.headline: The contract does not lapse
beats.text: Zev reminds Carl that his agreement with the programme is still in effect. Nothing signed on a floor above stops mattering because he has walked down a flight of stairs.
beats.gist: Zev reminds Carl that his agreement with the programme remains in effect after walking down stairs.

beats.headline: A third season, if they take it
beats.text: Quasar's second request in the negotiation for the Gate: an emergency licence for the programme to continue past the sixth floor. The kua-tin agree, on the condition that it is kept quiet; one mention out loud and it is negated. It is the equivalent of a third season, and not every secondary program is allowed to send its elites to the ninth floor. It would also give Sensation Entertainment an incentive to keep Carl alive. The producers have not actually agreed to anything. That was a bluff, and they have been unavailable.
beats.gist: Quasar requests an emergency licence for the programme to continue past the sixth floor.

beats.headline: Part one: Fort Freedom
beats.text: Signet gathers about seventy in a clearing around an old white tree: six were-warriors and their caterpillar, the ogre, forty bush elves, a talking tortoise, dryads, monkeys and forest creatures, plus Carl and Donut; the last to arrive are a pair of ursine. Then the quest drops. Part one of two. The leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up in the former river palace of the Naiad, now called Fort Freedom. Help Signet assault it and avenge her mother's assassination. The reward is part two, and every survivor of the assault will be 20% more willing to follow Carl's orders.
beats.gist: Signet gathers seventy creatures around an old white tree to assault Fort Freedom and avenge her mother.

beats.headline: Part one done, part two named
beats.text: The first act completes. The second arrives as a name: Queen Imogen of the high elves, Signet's half-sister, who will be at the masquerade at the close of this floor. The reward is the run of the high elf castle, thought to hold something that blunts Scolopendra's attack.
beats.gist: The first act completes and Queen Imogen of the high elves is named as the second act.

beats.headline: The second act closes
beats.text: A boss battle with crawlers, hunters, the queen and a goddess all in the same room. The high elves do not survive it. Imogen goes down, and the second season is complete.
beats.gist: Crawlers, hunters, the queen, and a goddess fight in one room; high elves die and Imogen falls.

beats.headline: Sold, with a season still owed
beats.text: Quasar warns Carl on arrival that the Dream has bought the programme out and intends to collect on the guaranteed third season.
beats.gist: Quasar warns Carl that the Dream bought the programme and intends to collect a third season.

recap.text: Carl suspects Signet's storyline is a programme called Vengeance of the Daughter, a name provided by Mordecai's friend Eklund. Carl poisons Grimaldi's vine with his blood to force a deal from the producers. He heals the vine, reads a Wisp Armor spellbook, and uses a cone of parasitic worms from Apollon the Mighty to talk Grimaldi into lifting Signet's banishment.

Zev reminds Carl that his agreement with the programme remains in effect. Quasar bluffs the kua-tin for an emergency licence to continue past the sixth floor, which would give Sensation Entertainment an incentive to keep Carl alive. Signet leads Carl, Donut, and a group including a talking tortoise and six were-warriors to assault Fort Freedom to avenge her mother. After the assault, Carl fights crawlers, hunters, a goddess, and Queen Imogen, leaving the high elves dead.
Quasar warns Carl on arrival that the Dream bought the programme out. The Dream intends to collect on the guaranteed third season.

entities.name: Stairwell
entities.tagline: A stairwell is an iron staircase wide enough for twenty, with warmth and light rising out of the ground. In a frozen city, it is the only warm place left.

beats.headline: The way down is lit from below
beats.text: Every floor is joined to the next by many of them, halving in number each floor down, and a crawler must find one and descend before that floor's time runs out. They are generally well lit, and the warmth comes up rather than down, so a crawler standing at the top is being invited by something that has already decided what happens next.
beats.gist: Stairwells join floors and halve in number each floor down before time runs out.

beats.headline: Don't go down early
beats.text: After the premiere the staircases down to the next level begin to populate, with a warning attached. Once down, a crawler cannot come back up, and this season anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse, out of sight while viewers lose interest and favorites drain away. The recommendation is to go down no earlier than six hours before the floor collapses; inside that window there is no stasis, and a head start over everyone already frozen at the bottom.
beats.gist: Staircases populate after the premiere with a warning that crawlers who descend early face stasis.

beats.headline: At the centre of a spiral
beats.text: The first stairwell down after a day's drive sits at the heart of a great round maze, and something rolls around its rings fast enough to shake the walls: pink, fleshy, as tall as the hallway, stinking of sewage. Mordecai had said the bosses would not guard stairwells until the fourth floor. The graffiti left by whoever got here first says otherwise: this road is safe, do not go deeper, or you activate the borough boss.
beats.gist: The first stairwell sits in a round maze where a pink, sewage-stinking creature shakes the walls.

beats.headline: Mobs do not go down
beats.text: A goblin shamanka told them once: mobs that climb down the stairs dissolve halfway. The guide said the same. So a level-93 rage elemental, which nobody here can kill, is lured across an oil slick into a stairwell hole, and the dungeon follows its own rules. The elemental dissolves with its health already in the red and a bomb going off beside it. Nobody is credited with the kill, and nobody gets the experience.
beats.gist: A level-93 rage elemental dissolves in a stairwell hole after crossing an oil slick.

beats.headline: The stairwell rule is patched
beats.text: The exploit gets its own paragraph in the next announcement. Yes, everyone just watched that rule get exploited on the recap. It was very clever and very exciting. It is not going to happen again. Effective immediately, any non-sapient mob that happens upon a stairwell will not be disintegrated. The same message says game guides may now explain the third floor's race and class selection.
beats.gist: The stairwell rule is patched so non-sapient mobs are not disintegrated and guides explain race and class.

beats.headline: Under the circus
beats.text: By morning the circus tents are gone, and so are the corpses and whatever a city boss might have dropped. In their place, in the middle of the park, is a staircase down to the fourth floor. It never showed on the map before, not even as one they could not reach, the way the Ball of Swine's did. Mordecai says many stairwells from here down only become visible once a quest is completed. This one had probably been sitting under Grimaldi the whole time.
beats.gist: A staircase to the fourth floor appears in the park after the circus tents and corpses vanish.

beats.headline: Mind the gap
beats.text: This one sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a small, decrepit building, and with the saferooms shut and the Desperado Club's back room sealed, it is the only way out of the blast. Crawlers have been leaving notes in the bars with stairwell locations. A floor ends for whoever goes down the moment they pull the handle at the bottom. The door there carries the usual oversized carving, and its properties read: Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.
beats.gist: A stairwell in a decrepit building provides the only way out of the blast.

beats.headline: The stairs hold; the doors do not
beats.text: A note from Milk in the Cookbook says a stairwell cannot go into an inventory or a saferoom, and one hit by an Utter Annihilation wand came through unscathed. The rules manual agrees: stairwells may be gated, never removed. The doors are another matter. A team of former Daughters in Turkey kill a crawler for his key, damage the door in the fight, and watch the key disappear. They dig down and find the chamber: a sealed rectangular room like a shipping container, with a straight wall where the door was. A Hole spell does nothing. Neither does Phase Through Walls.
beats.gist: A note from Milk and the rules manual state stairwells cannot be removed.

recap.text: Stairwells join floors and halve in number as crawlers descend. Anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse. A pink, fleshy creature stinking of sewage guards a stairwell at the heart of a round maze. A level-93 rage elemental dissolves in a stairwell hole, but the dungeon patches the rule so non-sapient mobs no longer disintegrate.

The circus tents and corpses vanish from the park, leaving a staircase down to the fourth floor. Mordecai says stairwells often become visible after a quest. Another stairwell sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a decrepit building. Crawlers leave notes in bars with stairwell locations. A door at the bottom reads Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.

Milk writes in the Cookbook that a stairwell cannot go into a saferoom or an inventory, and one survived a hit by an Utter Annihilation wand. The rules manual states stairwells may be gated but never removed. In Turkey, former Daughters kill a crawler for his key and damage the door, causing the key to disappear. They dig down to find a sealed rectangular room like a shipping container where a Hole spell and Phase Through Walls do nothing.

entities.name: Magic Missile
entities.tagline: Magic Missile came out of a tome in Donut's loot, and she had taught herself the spell before anyone could tell her how. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it only once.

beats.headline: Bolts from the eyes of a Persian
beats.text: Bolts of energy leave the caster’s eyes one after another, and the resemblance to a film about spaceships is close enough that nobody bothers to pretend otherwise. Princess Donut works it out for herself once Mordecai has switched her menus on, and from that point the question is never whether she will fire, only at what.
beats.gist: Energy bolts leave the caster's eyes; Princess Donut fires them after Mordecai switches her menus on.

beats.headline: Three to six
beats.text: At level five the spell lets the caster choose how much mana goes into each bolt, from three to six. At an intelligence of twenty-four that is eight missiles at three a piece, or a smaller number of bigger ones. A six leaves a level-two troglodyte a burnt-out husk. The man points out that a three would have done it. The cat's position is that anything about to bite her face off is getting a six.
beats.gist: At level five, Magic Missile lets the caster put three to six mana into each bolt.

recap.text: Bolts of energy leave the caster's eyes. Princess Donut learns the spell after Mordecai switches on her menus. At level five, she chooses to put three to six mana into each bolt. A six leaves a level-two troglodyte a burnt-out husk.

entities.name: Safe Room
entities.tagline: A safe room is always on the map, even under the fog of war, with restrooms, sleeping cubicles and, in some of them, food. There is no time limit, except the floor's own.

beats.headline: Green on a map that is otherwise unlit
beats.text: They sit throughout the dungeon and they show green on the minimap, which makes them the only honest thing on it. Inside there is food, a row of closet-sized rooms to sleep in, and three screens over the counter counting down to the collapse and to the premiere of the show. Each has a caretaker behind the counter.
beats.gist: Safe rooms show green on the minimap and contain food, sleeping rooms, three countdown screens, and caretakers.

beats.headline: A storm shelter with a mailbox
beats.text: Not every one is a restaurant. The first safe room on the second floor is a cavernous storm shelter with French signs on the restrooms, about fifty dusty cots and no Bopca: no food, no cookies, no vending machine, only bathrooms, showers and sinks, and screens on the far wall. By the screens is a black suburban mailbox on a pole, red flag and all. Carl tries the door and gets an error: Why would someone send you mail? It opens for the cat.
beats.gist: The first safe room on the second floor is a storm shelter with French restroom signs.

beats.headline: Closed an hour early
beats.text: Too many crawlers camped in safe rooms when the first floor collapsed, so the rule changes. All safe rooms and safe areas now close one hour before a floor collapses, and any crawler inside is teleported to just outside. A new timer appears under the collapse countdown, one hour faster. In a chicken restaurant full of the elderly, with a rage elemental hammering at the door, Carl and Brandon look at each other and think the same thing: it is time to give it up.
beats.gist: Safe rooms now close one hour before a floor collapses and teleport crawlers outside.

beats.headline: The Belly-Rubbed Pug
beats.text: On the third floor the saferooms are inns. This one is a renaissance-fair pub at the end of a dead-end alley, a pug in a top hat on the sign, the three screens as before and a Bopca called Gordo behind the counter. The sleeping rooms, only five of them, now cost ten gold a night, and the food costs money too. Mordecai teleports in with his trousers round his knees, addressing two girls and a grandma who are not there, vomits, sits in it, and passes out. Gordo's verdict: "You two are so dead."
beats.gist: Saferooms on the third floor are inns, including a renaissance-fair pub called The Belly-Rubbed Pug.

beats.headline: Lucia's saferoom loophole
beats.text: Lucia sets teleport traps inside saferoom doors, and the system allows it because the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. From inside a saferoom she can also cast a spell that teleports everyone in the room to a spot she chose in advance, where the room's safety no longer applies. It only works in her beautiful-woman form. A nerd kid at CrawlCon supplies the detail. Carl supplies a decoy, and the loophole takes Lucia to a spot where Vrah is already waiting.
beats.gist: Lucia uses a saferoom loophole to teleport Carl to Vrah, but a decoy redirects her.

beats.headline: The blood bar
beats.text: The failed creeper quest puts every saferoom and personal space on the floor under tenth-floor rules. A full blood bar buys ten hours inside. At zero the occupant is teleported to a random spot outside, and cannot enter a saferoom, guildhall or pub at all. The bar fills by killing, and it counts retroactively, so anyone who has killed nothing all floor starts empty. Moments after that, a hunter drops into the woods beside Carl and loses a leg to a raptor within seconds.
beats.gist: A failed creeper quest puts saferooms under tenth-floor rules, where blood bars buy time inside.

beats.headline: The Blood Bar
beats.text: The safe room is on a meter now. Walking in starts a Blood Bar: it begins full, it allows ten hours inside, and after that it has to be refilled the old-fashioned way, by killing things. Every box opened, every achievement read and every hour at the engineering table inside the room comes off the same ten hours.
beats.gist: The safe room uses a Blood Bar that allows ten hours inside before requiring kills to refill.

recap.text: Safe rooms show green on the minimap and contain food, closet-sized sleeping rooms, and screens counting down to the collapse and the show premiere. One safe room is a storm shelter with French signs on the restrooms and a black suburban mailbox that opens only for the cat. All safe rooms now close one hour before a floor collapses. In a chicken restaurant with a rage elemental hammering at the door, Carl and Brandon decide to give it up.

On the third floor, saferooms are inns. One is a renaissance-fair pub with a pug in a top hat on the sign and a Bopca called Gordo behind the counter. Mordecai teleports in with his trousers round his knees, vomits, and passes out. Gordo says you two are so dead.

Lucia sets teleport traps inside saferoom doors and casts a spell in her beautiful-woman form to teleport people to a spot where safety does not apply. Carl uses a decoy to send Lucia to a spot where Vrah waits. A failed creeper quest puts saferooms under tenth-floor rules, where a full blood bar buys ten hours of stay. A hunter drops into the woods and loses a leg to a raptor.
The safe room runs on a Blood Bar that allows ten hours inside. Killing things refills the bar. Opening boxes, reading achievements, and spending hours at the engineering table reduce the ten hours.

tagline.text: Bopca Protectors are magical, gnome-like creatures who exist solely to watch over safe rooms. They scrub the toilets and cook the food, they are surly and smelly, and they never wash their hands.

A Bopca Protector runs every safe room, like Wendita behind the counter of a red-and-white fast-food restaurant here. The good ones, like Tally and Sebastian, are excellent cooks who treat the cat like royalty.

beats.headline: The protector behind the counter
beats.text: Magical, gnome-like, hairy, and posted to watch over safe rooms. They do everything from scrubbing the toilets to cooking the food; they are surly, they are smelly, and they never wash their hands. The first one they meet is called Tally.
beats.gist: Tally is a surly, smelly, hairy, gnome-like Bopca who scrubs toilets and never washes their hands.

beats.headline: They came, and Tally went
beats.text: Tally comes out from behind the counter to watch the premiere at the booth, and he does not like last season. The other corporation broke people into groups and told them their loved ones would be safe if they killed the others. The loved ones were safe, he says, and not safe; that company saps a planet dry and leaves it without air. Borant at least gives people a chance. He was never a crawler. Sometimes they offer to take people instead of mining a world. They came, and he went. Very long ago.
beats.gist: Tally watches the premiere and says Borant gives people a chance unlike the other corporation.

beats.headline: Sebastian and the hairbrush
beats.text: The Peruvian Taco Bell has a Protector named Sebastian, level twenty-one, and a cat with a charisma of forty-one walks in and he is lost. The man gets a Peruvian beer and a T-bone steak. The cat gets the Protector: he sits beside her through the third episode brushing her hair with one of his own brushes, which he gave her after her third shower.
beats.gist: A cat with a charisma of forty-one gets a level twenty-one Protector named Sebastian.

recap.text: Tally is a surly, smelly, hairy, gnome-like Protector who scrubs toilets and cooks food in safe rooms. Tally tells of a corporation that saps planets dry and leaves them without air. In a Peruvian Taco Bell, a level twenty-one Protector named Sebastian brushes a cat's hair with his own brush.

entities.name: Brindle Grub
entities.tagline: Brindle Grubs are the janitors of the second floor. They eat whatever gets killed, and the more they eat, the bigger they grow.

beats.headline: Janitor duty
beats.text: On the second floor the rats are yesterday’s news and the grubs are the janitors. The more monsters killed in an area, the more the grubs eat; the more they eat, the bigger they get. Grubs are easy to kill. Once they turn up in the pupa stage, move on, because their older siblings are not.
beats.gist: Grubs act as janitors on the second floor, growing larger as they eat killed monsters.

beats.headline: Five thousand to a quadrant
beats.text: A guildmaster checks his menu and confirms it: they are being spawned. The system is making anywhere from one to fifteen grubs whenever a corpse is created, with no janitor mobs nearby, and with no corpses about they hunt crawlers instead. The seven hundred and fifty fried in a boss's cage count. Dead grubs make more grubs. There is a cap of five thousand per quadrant, and Carl and Donut have already hit it. The level twos neither bite nor give experience. They squeak, they wriggle, and they eat their own dead.
beats.gist: A guildmaster confirms the system spawns one to fifteen grubs per corpse, capped at five thousand.

beats.headline: Half as many hornets
beats.text: The System AI decides the Brindled Vespas are proliferating too aggressively and halves the number in the dungeon. Their spitting acid is adjusted down. Slightly. New grubs keep generating whenever a corpse is created, but each now has only a fifty percent chance of reaching the pupa stage. On the same recap, Lucia Mar smashes a vespa to pieces with her mace while its acid sizzles two inches from her head, on a personal shield.
beats.gist: The System AI halves the number of Brindled Vespas and slightly lowers their spitting acid.

recap.text: Brindle grubs act as janitors that grow larger as they eat killed monsters. The system spawns one to fifteen grubs per corpse, and Carl and Donut hit the cap of five thousand per quadrant. The System AI halves the number of Brindled Vespas and lowers their acid. Lucia Mar smashes a vespa with her mace.

entities.name: Clockwork Triplicate
entities.tagline: Clockwork Triplicate splits a pet or minion into three real copies, each with a mind of its own. After about a minute, the copies fall apart into gears and go up in smoke.

beats.headline: Three of something there was one of
beats.text: Cast on a pet or a minion, the target splits into three. The copies are real, look right and act with minds of their own, and after a minute they fall apart into gears and servos and go up in smoke. Donut learns it from a spellbook the same evening her Earth box turns up a cat tree and a scented candle, which is roughly the level of seriousness the dungeon brings to its gifts.
beats.gist: Donut learns a spell that splits a pet or minion into three gear-filled copies for one minute.

beats.headline: Two Mongos and a bloody letter
beats.text: On a roof across the alley from the magistrate's building, Donut casts it on Mongo and pulls the original back into his carrier. The two copies squeak their disappointment and then do the work. One swallows the Mysterious Letter, which carries a lich's eavesdropping spell, and the pair leap across the alley and up a full story to the magistrate's roof, howling. Anyone listening through the letter should now place the crawlers overhead. Carl had not believed they could jump that far. The real party is crouched a building away when he presses the detonator.
beats.gist: Donut casts a spell on Mongo to create two copies that swallow a lich's eavesdropping letter.

recap.text: Donut learns a spell from a book on the evening she receives a cat tree and a scented candle. She casts the spell on Mongo, splitting him into three. One copy swallows a Mysterious Letter carrying a lich's eavesdropping spell, and the copies leap to the magistrate's roof howling. Carl presses a detonator while the real party crouches a building away.

entities.name: Jikininki
entities.tagline: Jikininki are the most common ghouls in the Iron Tangle, the best-behaved and the most insatiable. They will generally leave you alone, as long as you are not bleeding, you do not litter, and you stay out of their personal space.

beats.headline: They are waiting when the doors open
beats.text: The commonest ghoul on the line, and by the System’s own account the most tractable of them, which says more about the others than it does about these. The court meets its first pair in the first minutes on the new floor, by diving into their train car to escape a flood of Drek babies, before anyone has established what the rules of the place are.
beats.gist: The court dives into a train car to escape Drek babies and meets two tractable Jikininki ghouls.

beats.headline: Swarming the wreckage
beats.text: At the bottom of the pit above Abyss Station lie thousands of crashed train cars and hundreds of fires, and the janitor ghouls are down there, swarming the debris like ants. Train after train bursts from the portals in the walls and tumbles in on top of them. None of them has an engine car.
beats.gist: Janitor ghouls swarm crashed train cars and fires at the bottom of the pit above Abyss Station.

recap.text: The court dives into a train car to escape a flood of Drek babies and meets a pair of Jikininki ghouls. Thousands of janitor ghouls swarm crashed train cars and fires at the bottom of a pit above Abyss Station. Trains without engine cars burst from portals in the walls and tumble on top of them.

tagline.text: According to a train engineer, the Kravyad handle the rail employees who get off at station 435 and go through the portal home, and anyone who takes that path loses time and memory.
The Kravyad wait at station 435, where the rail employees get off. Madison, who works above them, insists that they are not bosses at all but part of human resources.

beats.headline: Whatever they are, they are at station 435
beats.text: A few dozen of them work directly under the line’s management, and they are stationed where the employees leave the train. Whether they count as a boss or as scenery depends entirely on who is describing them, which is a distinction the dungeon is happy to leave unsettled for as long as it is useful.
beats.gist: Dozens of workers at station 435 are either bosses or scenery.

recap.text: A few dozen workers stay at station 435 where employees leave the train. The dungeon leaves it unsettled whether they count as a boss or as scenery.

tagline.text: Skyfowl are what Mordecai was born as: going by the photograph of his brother, a golden, eagle-like creature with angel's wings folded on its back.

Skyfowl look like eagles, with feet and wings but no arms. On the fifth floor Mordecai is one again, a rock edge skyfowl cleric with clipped wings, in the first body close to his own in a very long time.

beats.headline: The guide's own people
beats.text: Eagle-headed, and by the guide's account his own people, who tend to outlast humans because they roll with whatever comes. He was born one and was a centurion before he took another race, and on the fifth floor the dungeon puts him back in something like the shape: a rock edge skyfowl cleric, wings clipped, the first body near his real one in a very long time.
beats.gist: Mordecai is a rock edge skyfowl cleric with clipped wings.

recap.text: Mordecai was born an eagle-headed skyfowl and served as a centurion. The dungeon puts him back in a rock edge skyfowl cleric shape with clipped wings. This body is the first near his real one in a long time.

tagline.text: A Tummy Acher is one of the caged pets for sale: a meatball with two legs and a mohawk.
A Tummy Acher is a pet-class mob, once a parasite in the guts of titans, that grows stronger every time it dies. This one bonded with Carl over a single bowl of chowder.

beats.headline: Died five times, and stronger for it
beats.text: A pet-class mob. The System’s notice for one that has not yet bonded to a crawler reads like a card on a cage: this one has died five times, and its stats are all buffed by 125% because of it. It has five weaknesses, which can be examined only by whoever bonds with it or holds it in a carrier.
beats.gist: A pet-class mob has died five times, buffing its stats by 125%.

beats.headline: Bonded on one bowl of chowder
beats.text: Carl lets the level-one tummy acher out onto the table, and it hops straight into Mongo's open mouth. Mongo swallows, then yaks it back up, giggling. Carl's food box now serves everything chowder style, so his breakfast sandwich comes crumbled into seafood soup; he puts the bowl down, the meatball dives in, growls at Mongo, and its dot turns orange. One bowl, and bonded. Then it pushes the bowl over to Mongo. The naming window will not close until Louis comes up with a knight's name built on Ren's.
beats.gist: Carl lets a level-one tummy acher hop into Mongo's open mouth.

recap.text: A pet-class mob has died five times, buffing its stats by 125%. Carl lets the level-one tummy acher onto a table, and it hops into Mongo's open mouth. The meatball dives into a bowl of seafood soup, growls at Mongo, and bonds for the cost of one bowl of chowder. Louis must find a knight's name built on Ren's to close the naming window.

tagline.text: Ping is a five-mana spell that marks everything that is neither a crawler nor red-tagged. Everything it finds hears it, and the System calls it a tool for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming.
Also known as "Here piggy, piggy" and the Night Dread, Ping finds almost nothing in a castle full of robots, which is exactly how the drake stands out.

beats.headline: Here piggy, piggy
beats.text: Five mana, and it tells you where everything is that is neither a crawler nor red-tagged, out past the edge of the map. Everything it finds hears the ping, though not where it came from, which is why the System files it under names like the Night Dread and says it is for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming. In a castle full of robots it turns up almost nothing, which is how a drake stands out: orange on the map, somebody's pet.
beats.gist: Ping costs five mana and reveals non-crawler, non-red-tagged things beyond the map, alerting the quarry.

recap.text: Ping costs five mana and reveals everything past the map edge that is not a crawler or red-tagged. The found targets hear the ping, so the System names the spell the Night Dread. In a castle of robots, the spell finds almost nothing except a drake, which appears orange on the map as somebody's pet.

tagline.text: Sluggalos are slugs that pour out of infected mercenaries every few minutes, hundreds of them in a room full of blood. Imani calls them punk rock, and Carl corrects her.
The System files them as Pox Slugs, but the Sluggalos come out of the boils of the SlugPox in clown makeup, with hatchets and a rowdy culture of their own, and throw themselves at the demons.

beats.headline: Filed as Pox Slugs, and unbothered by it
beats.text: The System first registers them as Pox Slugs, which is accurate and entirely misses the point. They come out of the boils of the SlugPox, they arrive with a crude and rowdy culture already assembled, and they throw themselves at the demons with the enthusiasm of people who cannot believe their luck at being included.
beats.gist: The System registers Sluggalos as Pox Slugs who emerge from boils and attack demons with enthusiasm.

beats.headline: Credit to Kandy Newton
beats.text: System message: the Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen, and credit for the kill goes to Kandy "Bigs" Newton of the Princess Posse. She is a level-29 sluggalette the size of a bulldog, with wisps of pink hair and a hatchet growing out of the top of her head, and she came out of Carl's back when his slugpox broke loose. The Blood Sultanate is defeated, its assets passing to Donut and Katia and on to the Posse. Her next moves are to swing at Samantha and to try to bury the hatchet in Baroness Victory's leg, which it passes straight through.
beats.gist: Kandy Bigs Newton, a bulldog-sized sluggalette with a head-hatchet, kills the Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate.

beats.headline: The code
beats.text: Bigs, sitting on Dong's head and swinging her hatchet at Carl, lays out the sluggalo code: unity, support, family, and kneecapping. By that standard Carl has provided none of the four, which in her reckoning makes him the problem. He agrees with her, which she was not expecting. They settle on a word for what people are when they keep helping each other anyway, and the word is Real Gs. She slimes off, leaving an orange streak on Dong's head, and tells Carl she is not the one he owes an apology.
beats.gist: Bigs sits on Dong's head and tells Carl the sluggalo code is unity, support, family, and kneecapping.

beats.headline: Lil' Mello Haze
beats.text: The boil on Carl's back bursts in the Vendor Village and delivers a level thirty slug named Lil' Mello Haze, higher level than Bigs but smaller, on account of Carl currently being a dachshund. He wears a backward baseball cap hanging off his eye sockets and has a mace head for a tail instead of the usual hatchet. He greets his father as daddy man, is called to heel, ignores it, and wanders off in the opposite direction. The father's barking does not help.
beats.gist: A boil on Carl's back bursts in the Vendor Village and delivers Lil' Mello Haze.

beats.headline: Down onto the stands
beats.text: The bay doors of the Reaver transport open over the judging stands and the sluggalos come down on the audience: bankers, politicians and elites, masked, bound and unable to fight back. The smallest of the small, the lowest form of dungeon NPC, slaughtering them one by one. It is the last thing on the Vengeance float, and it was planned. Bigs calls it unity, support, family and kneecapping.
beats.gist: Reaver transport bay doors open and sluggalos slaughter masked, bound elites on the judging stands.

recap.text: The System registers Sluggalos as Pox Slugs. They come out of the boils of the SlugPox with a crude and rowdy culture. They throw themselves at demons with enthusiasm.

A system message credits Kandy Bigs Newton for the kill of the Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate. Kandy is a level-29 sluggalette the size of a bulldog with a hatchet growing from her head who came out of Carl's back. Donut and Katia take the assets of the Blood Sultanate and pass them to the Posse. Kandy swings at Samantha and tries to bury her hatchet in Baroness Victory's leg.

Bigs sits on Dong's head and swings a hatchet while explaining the sluggalo code of unity, support, family, and kneecapping. A boil on Carl's back bursts in the Vendor Village to deliver Lil' Mello Haze, a level thirty slug with a mace head for a tail and a backward baseball cap. Sluggalos drop from a Reaver transport onto masked bankers and politicians in the judging stands to slaughter them.

tagline.text: A ManTauR, according to the System, is half human and half human, and bred for strength and dexterity, which here means driving trains.
Where a centaur has a horse, a mantaur has a second human half, and the System calls it one of the weirdest of all the 'taurs.

beats.headline: Of all the ’taurs, this one
beats.text: Centaurs, bisontaurs, rhinotaurs: the dungeon has a long catalogue of things joined at the waist to other things, and this is the entry the System itself flags as peculiar. They turn up from the fourth floor down, and they keep company with Club Vanquisher.
beats.gist: The System flags the Mantaur as peculiar among the waist-joined creatures that appear from the fourth floor.

recap.text: The dungeon has a catalogue of centaurs, bisontaurs, and rhinotaurs joined at the waist. The System flags the Mantaur as peculiar. These creatures turn up from the fourth floor down and keep company with Club Vanquisher.

entities.name: Protective Shell

tagline.text: Protective Shell comes with a pair of enchanted boxers: once every thirty hours, a sphere that no mob can enter, lasting twenty seconds and growing with the wearer's intelligence. It does not move with you.
Protective Shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast. Cast it inside a speeding train, and it rolls back through the cars like a bulldozer, pushing every mob before it.

entities.description: A favorite of frontline tanks and castle guards, the expensive and rare Protective Shell spell shields the caster and anyone within the sphere from a mob's physical presence or physical attacks. This spell does not protect against magic or against non-corporeal entities. Unlike the more popular Shield spell, this spell does not move with you. This spell's area of effect remains static once cast, unimpeded by your physical surroundings.

beats.headline: Inside a pair of boxers
beats.text: A boss box yields a white pair of boxers covered in little red hearts, the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers: plus two Constitution, and the wearer may cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell once every thirty hours. No mana; take the boxers off and the spell goes with them. A sphere with a radius of three metres plus half a metre per point of Intelligence, lasting twenty seconds. Mordecai had it during his own crawl and starts to explain its fantastic secondary effect, when an admin warning cuts him off.
beats.gist: A boss box yields heart-covered boxers that cast a Protective Shell without mana.

beats.headline: A dog at the end of its leash
beats.text: First cast, in a hallway, with a rage elemental coming for the residents. The glowing half-sphere fills the corridor floor to ceiling, and the monster flies back like a charging dog reaching the end of its leash. It charges again; its badger head gets through, but its claws cannot. Crawler Carl's ears pop as he runs out of the area toward the safe room. Twenty seconds, and he spent five of them being dumbfounded that it worked.
beats.gist: Carl casts Protective Shell in a hallway against a rage elemental, creating a glowing half-sphere.

beats.headline: Lions off a bug zapper
beats.text: Six mold lions pounce at once in a dark street. Crawler Carl slams the shell down as Crawler Donut's Confusing Fog billows out, and the lions bounce off it like fireflies off a bug zapper, each ricocheting in a different direction, howling. It holds long enough for Carl to punch into a lion's chest with his gauntlet and pull its heart out. The shell fizzles just as the reanimated lion gets back to its feet.
beats.gist: Six mold lions pounce in a dark street, but bounce off Carl's Protective Shell.

beats.headline: The boxers, upgraded
beats.text: An upgrade scroll goes onto the boxers. The spell itself does not change; the garment gets plus five Dexterity, plus five Intelligence, three more Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit, which permits one layer of clothing over the crotch and so rules out trousers. Mordecai calls them probably the most valuable item Crawler Carl owns. Five points of Intelligence is two and a half more metres of radius.
beats.gist: An upgrade scroll gives the boxers plus five Dexterity, Intelligence, and three Constitution.

beats.headline: Left behind on the tracks
beats.text: The secondary effect, applied. Trapped in a speeding subway car with mobs breaking through the doors, Crawler Carl checks that the track is straight and casts. The shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast along the track, so the train carries on through it, and it rolls down the cars, sixteen to twenty, pushing every mob before it like a bulldozer and squashing them into paste against the first surface they meet.
beats.gist: Carl casts Protective Shell in a speeding subway car, pushing mobs like a bulldozer into paste.

beats.headline: The train drives into it
beats.text: The plan for the Nightmare Express: stand on the track in the tunnel, cast the shell as the train arrives, and let Crawler Donut's Puddle Jumper take them a quarter of a mile down the line. They cut it close. The train roars through the spell, and every red-tagged monster aboard slams into its wall and is pushed backward. The train then speeds up, and they have to run for the platform.

beats.headline: The floor was the monster
beats.text: Cast on a stairway as a door explodes inward, the shell sweeps the sand off the floor of the room like a broom and uncovers glass beneath. Suddenly the whole room is red on the map. The sand is a mob, and there is no second cast today.
beats.gist: A shell sweeps sand off a floor to uncover glass, revealing the sand is a mob.

beats.headline: Straight down a city boss
beats.text: Swallowed along with a submarine, Crawler Carl casts in the throat of an enormous shark. The static sphere, about twelve metres across by now, shoots away as the shark swims on. He hoped for a bullet through the brain. Instead the boss stops dead, as if it had hit a wall; the top of its mouth peels back over its own eyes, teeth shatter, and the immovable spell pushes it down into the ocean floor. Grievously wounded, it is not yet dead.
beats.gist: Carl casts a static sphere in a shark's throat, pushing the boss into the ocean floor.

beats.headline: Train the spell, upgrade the shorts
beats.text: The tier-four training room installed for Crawler Carl while he is held off the floor lists spells that come from equipment alongside the ordinary ones. Train Protective Shell there, and it is the equipment that gets upgraded: the boxers, in this case. The room also trains workshop tables without them being present, which Crawler Carl rates as its most valuable feature.
beats.gist: Carl trains Protective Shell in a tier-four training room, which upgrades his boxers and trains workshop tables.

beats.headline: Straight up, not sideways
beats.text: The frog-lizard boss on the hill had a weak belly and a description hinting it should be rolled over. Crawler Carl cast too close and at the wrong angle, and the monster went straight up into the night sky instead of sideways. Crawler Donut's fireball met its stomach as it fell back down, and it landed on the shield in flames. Now, in a saferoom, the achievement catches up: Uprooted notes that a rooted-in-place boss was moved, and hopes he remembers how.
beats.gist: Carl casts Protective Shell at a wrong angle and sends a frog-lizard boss straight up.

beats.headline: A crater of bugs
beats.text: A literal wave of thrashing bugs falls on Crawler Carl in the fight with a deity. He slams the shell down. Bugs, elves, dinosaurs and a few hunters rocket away in every direction. With the Intelligence he has now, the shell is huge; it leaves a crater with only crawlers and corpses in the middle, and Imani uses the gap to heal whoever she can reach.
beats.gist: Carl slams the Protective Shell down, rocketing bugs, elves, dinosaurs and hunters away to let Imani heal.

recap.text: A boss box yields Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, white with little red hearts, which add two Constitution and cast a level-fifteen Protective Shell every thirty hours. The spell creates a sphere with a radius of three metres plus half a metre per point of Intelligence for twenty seconds. Carl casts it in a hallway against a rage elemental, and the monster flies back like a charging dog reaching the end of its leash.

Six mold lions pounce in a dark street. Carl slams the shell down while Donut uses Confusing Fog, and the lions bounce off like fireflies off a bug zapper. Carl punches into a lion's chest with his gauntlet and pulls out its heart. An upgrade scroll gives the boxers plus five Dexterity, plus five Intelligence, three Constitution, and the Freeballing benefit. Mordecai calls them probably the most valuable item Carl owns.

Carl casts a shell on a straight track, and the spell stays in place as a speeding subway car carries on through it. The shell rolls down sixteen to twenty cars, pushing mobs like a bulldozer and squashing them into paste. Carl and Donut cast the shell as the Nightmare Express arrives. The train roars through the spell, and every red-tagged monster slams into the wall and is pushed backward.

Carl casts the shell on a stairway as a door explodes, sweeping sand off a floor to uncover glass. The sand is a mob. Carl casts the shell in the throat of an enormous shark. The twelve-metre sphere pushes the shark into the ocean floor, shattering its teeth and peeling its mouth back over its eyes.

Crawler Carl trains Protective Shell in a tier-four training room, which upgrades his boxers and trains workshop tables without them being present. He casts the spell at a frog-lizard boss, sending the monster straight up into the night sky. In a fight with a deity, Carl slams the shell down to rocket bugs, elves, and dinosaurs away, leaving a crater that Imani uses to heal.

tagline.text: The world froze, heavy metal played, and Carl's face appeared in the air with Death Challenge! stamped across it in blood. The announcer promised the live death of a celebrated crawler.
A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event. The AI put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and Borant has appealed over how slowly it moved the odds.

beats.headline: The world freezes, the music starts
beats.text: Carl tumbles out of a portal into Trainyard E beside a glowing mantaur, a Mimic Rex's mouth opens in front of him, and the world stops. Music starts: heavy metal, bass-driven. A framed graphic of Carl's face appears in the air with Death Challenge! stamped across it, blood running from the words. The announcer promises the death of a celebrated crawler, live, and asks which lucky monster gets to kill him. Carl, frozen, has one thought about it, and it is a swear word.
beats.gist: Carl tumbles into Trainyard E beside a glowing mantaur as a Mimic Rex opens its mouth.

beats.headline: Two contenders and a sponsor
beats.text: On the right, a level-90 Mimic Rex, city boss and crawler-killer champion of the floor with over 23,000 deaths. On the left, Grull, and for the first time on Dungeon Crawler World his sponsor: Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire, once thought dead, interviewed on screen telling the worms to try harder. The world stays frozen through the portraits while Donut gallops toward the trainyard on Mongo. Then the announcer tells everyone to get their bets in, and the world unfreezes.
beats.gist: A level-90 Mimic Rex faces Grull and his sponsor, Prince Maestro, in a gambling event.

beats.headline: No announcement at the end
beats.text: Grull splits the mimic in half, steps on Carl, and runs off after a second Carl who is Katia in disguise. Carl lives through the god's stamping on Mordecai's Special Brew. A mutilated mantaur, thrown into the portal with one second left on its summoning, takes the god away mid-attack. Then the music stops. There is no additional announcement, the way there usually is. There is only the chugging of a train, and a whole page of notifications.
beats.gist: Grull splits a mimic, steps on Carl, and chases Katia disguised as a second Carl.

beats.headline: What the odds were
beats.text: On Odette's couch it is explained. A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event: viewers in systems where gambling is legal bet on outcomes, general or specific, each at its own odds. The AI put Carl's general survival at fifty to one. Plenty of viewers thought that was a good bet, and the odds slid less than you would expect. Borant has filed an appeal over how slowly the AI moved the spread. Odette made a good amount of credits.
beats.gist: Odette explains on her couch that a Death Challenge is a pop-up gambling event for viewers.

recap.text: Carl tumbles into Trainyard E as the world freezes and heavy metal music starts. A Mimic Rex with 23,000 deaths and Grull, sponsored by Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire, are the contenders to kill him. Grull splits the mimic in half and steps on Carl, who survives because he is on Mordecai's Special Brew. A mutilated mantaur takes Grull away mid-attack. Odette explains that the AI set Carl's survival odds at fifty to one for this pop-up gambling event.

tagline.text: Pustule once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, and her mother died of it. You cannot bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, she says, without doing a little dying.

Astrid has unleashed the vorpals from behind the Desperado Club's Do Not Enter door, as a last resort against a feral demon loose in the club. She will not say what they are, only that they are going to kill everything.

According to Mordecai, vorpal is a condition, not a species. Vorpals are deputised by the gods and drawn to demons, stronger and angrier the nearer one is, and liable to blow themselves up rather than lose.

beats.headline: One muskrat, one mother
beats.text: A hobgoblin at the Silk Road, midway through pricing hob-lobbers, mentions that she once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat. To teach the warlord a lesson, her mother said; the daughter suspects another reason. A few minutes on, Princess Donut hopes the mother won't be biting her head off too. No danger, says the hobgoblin: she died. It was a vorpal muskrat. You can't bite the head off a vorpal muskrat without doing a little dying in the process. Nobody asks what vorpal means.
beats.gist: A hobgoblin explains that biting a vorpal muskrat's head causes the biter to die.

beats.headline: Fifteen things behind a door
beats.text: In a secret corridor of the Desperado Club, past fifty traps, some of them demon snares, is the abandoned practice arena of the defunct Demon Tamer's Guild, and in it fifteen red-tagged monsters nobody has identified. The paper sign on the padlocked door: Warning. Do Not Enter. Extreme, You're-Going-To-Die-In-A-Lot-Of-Pain Danger. Posted by Management. Parties have gone in. None came out. Carl, setting an ambush in that same corridor, walls the door off with two blast-resistant panels and sandbags, on a feeling.
beats.gist: Carl walls off a door to a practice arena with sandbags and two blast-resistant panels.

beats.headline: The last resort
beats.text: A feral demon out of the Nothing is loose on the middle floor, eating guards, and the club cannot kill her. Astrid pulls the trigger: "I had to unleash the vorpals." Carl asks what those are. It does not matter, she says; they are going to kill everything, so flee or hide. Then she frets about what is taking them so long. Meanwhile, guards heading down that corridor keep landing on Carl's teleport traps. The vorpals won't go up to the top floor, she adds, not sounding sure.
beats.gist: Astrid unleashes vorpals to kill a feral demon eating guards on the middle floor.

beats.headline: Deputised by the gods
beats.text: Mordecai, asked in chat, has not seen these in a while. Vorpal is a condition, not a species. Feral means touched by the Nothing; vorpal means deputised by the gods, or better, turned into suicide bombers. Any race, sometimes hidden until a demon is near. Celestial guards and foot soldiers. The closer the demon, the stronger and angrier they get; they sense it, go to it, and draw its aggro. If one thinks it is losing, it explodes, and everybody in the room is dead with it. Stay away.
beats.gist: Vorpal is a condition where gods turn any race into suicide bombers that explode near demons.

beats.headline: Carl opens his own wall
beats.text: The only thing between the vorpals and the club is the wall Carl built. So he sends a door-opening bot down the hidden hallway, programmed with a sixty-second delay to undo his own bracers and burrow through his own sandbags, and goes upstairs. Some minutes on, a buzzsaw sound rises through the floor of the strip club, and yellow fluid sprays through a hole in the boards. The demon screams a name, and a curse, and stops. The vorpals have found her.
beats.gist: Carl sends a door-opening bot to burrow through his sandbags and the vorpals find the demon.

beats.headline: Still loose downstairs
beats.text: The demon is dead and the vorpals are still tearing through the lower level. Now that they have bathed in demon blood they are supposed to dissipate back to the celestial realm, which is fine in theory and silent on timing. Crawler Carl keeps an eye on Damascus Steel, crying on the floor of the club, because Damascus is a demon class and his presence is a problem with those things still in the building.
beats.gist: Vorpals tear through the lower level after killing a demon and before dissipating to the celestial realm.

recap.text: A hobgoblin at the Silk Road tells Princess Donut that her mother once bit the head off a vorpal muskrat. The mother died in the process. Nobody asks what vorpal means.

Carl walls off a padlocked door in the Desperado Club containing fifteen red-tagged monsters. Astrid unleashes vorpals, suicide bombers deputised by the gods, to kill a feral demon. Carl uses a door-opening bot to remove his sandbags and panels. The vorpals kill the demon, but Carl watches Damascus Steel because Damascus is a demon class.

tagline.text: T'Ghee is a card game from the home planet of Allister, the thirteenth edition's author: somewhere between chess and go fish, and part of his people's meditation-based religion. His copy of the Cookbook came as a deck of the cards.
Each squad leader has twenty flags. Plant one in a living thing below five percent health, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem card that fights for whoever summons it. Lost flags are not replaced.

A T'Ghee deck holds totems, utility, snare, mystic and special cards. Four are drawn when combat starts and one more every ten seconds, and a squad leader cannot use spells or inventory until the deck is spent.
A squad flag does not check what it is stabbed into, and it works on a dying crawler just as well as on a monster.

beats.headline: Allister's deck of cards
beats.text: The Cookbook manifests differently for each owner. For Allister, author of the thirteenth edition, it came as a massive deck of playing cards from his home planet, for a game called T'Ghee. From the little he wrote about it, a mix of chess and go fish; also part of his people's meditation-based religion, which made it easy for him to spend hours studying the cards.
beats.gist: The Cookbook manifests for Allister as a deck of T'Ghee cards from his home planet.

beats.headline: Two vampires in the deck
beats.text: Allister, on vampires: his culture has them too, and his T'Ghee deck contains two vampiric forms. Both represent death and the end of days. One is deliberate, thirst-based evil. The other, the Plague Bearer, is a study in how poor actions ripple through time, amplify, and doom everyone. The vampires on the floor he is writing from, he thinks, are a combination of the two. It is strange, he writes, that the traditions are so different yet the same.
beats.gist: Allister writes that his T'Ghee deck contains two vampiric forms representing death and the end of days.

beats.headline: Twenty flags a squad
beats.text: Floor announcement. Each squad leader receives twenty flags bearing a logo the system designed. Plant one in a living thing below five per cent health, noncorporeal included, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem, a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point depending on level and temperament. Rip the totem in two to dismiss it. Trade them, steal them. Lost flags are not replaced. Every surviving squad keeps one card when the floor collapses. Carl's breath catches: he knows the word from the Cookbook.
beats.gist: Squad leaders receive twenty system-designed logo flags to create T'Ghee totem minions from low-health living things.

beats.headline: Like the stuffed animals
beats.text: Mordecai's gloss on the announcement: T'Ghee totems are like Bautista's stuffed animals, only in the form of large playing cards. Like Carl's tarot cards, actually. Reusable even when the summoned monster dies. He has seen them used a few different ways over the seasons, so they are going to have to wait for the next announcement. Carl, who has read Allister, notes that for its inventor T'Ghee was a religion and had nothing to do with capturing monsters.
beats.gist: T'Ghee totems are large playing cards that summon reusable monsters.

beats.headline: The rules, at length
beats.text: The full rules arrive. Six totems minimum per deck. Five card types: totems, utility, snare, mystic, special. Four cards drawn when combat starts and one more every ten seconds; one discard, recharging every thirty. A squad leader in deck combat loses spells and inventory until the deck is spent, and most totems may not attack an enemy leader while enemy totems stand, so the squad guards the leader. Against an opponent holding a deck, deck combat is compulsory. Saferooms gain practice arenas, for a fee.
beats.gist: The full rules for T'Ghee cards arrive.

beats.headline: Sacred to someone
beats.text: On the road to a cemetery, Sister Ines says what she has been holding in: all of this is a mockery of their faiths and legends, the stories stripped of meaning and made shiny, holy things mixed with fictions nobody ever believed. They do not care. Crawler Carl gives her a moment, and says it is what they do. He does not say the rest aloud. The cards themselves were sacred to the aliens the idea was stolen from. They were never meant to be used like this.
beats.gist: Sister Ines calls the T'Ghee cards a mockery of faith; Carl says it is what they do.

beats.headline: A flag in a person
beats.text: A squad flag does not check what it is stabbed into. Sister Ines drives one into the neck of her dying friend Paz, who has just asked to be let go, and Paz becomes a card, green, common, in her hand. She looks as stunned as everyone else that it worked. Behind her, the fountain bubbles over, and two goddesses make an appearance in the realm.
beats.gist: Sister Ines stabs a squad flag into the neck of Paz, turning her into a green common card.

beats.headline: Millions of work hours
beats.text: An achievement, at length. Borant's proposal for this season included an outline of the eighth floor as a T'Ghee card game; artists, engineers and writers spent millions of work hours designing and balancing it for thousands of players at once, and Cascadia, the executive producer, is on the edge. Most crawlers keep ending card fights before either side draws. Crawler Carl's review: a half-assed YuGiOh! ripoff duct-taped together on an Adderall bender, and no card game is fair when players draw from different pools.
beats.gist: Borant proposed a T'Ghee card game that artists, engineers and writers spent millions of work hours designing.

beats.headline: A card called The Inevitable
beats.text: Allister again, writing about a goddess the dwarves call the Downward Spiral: an earth and water goddess who punishes those who abuse her world and the weakest in it, a trickster, jealous of mortals, forever moving nations like chess pieces. In his religion, he writes, there is a T'Ghee card that represents such a figure. It is called The Inevitable.
beats.gist: Allister writes about The Inevitable, a T'Ghee card representing the Downward Spiral, a jealous trickster goddess.

beats.headline: One card to keep
beats.text: Each surviving squad may keep a single card past the collapse. Princess Donut had meant it to be Lazarus or the Golden Combo, and now offers a third: a card of Paz, in case there is a way to set him free. Crawler Carl remembers what Paz said the last time he was summoned. Not that one, and not the Golden Combo either. The Paz card is ripped in half on his shoulder.
beats.gist: Surviving squads keep one card; Carl rips the Paz card in half on his shoulder.

beats.headline: The Open Wound
beats.text: Allister, on the Immortality condition: an immortal's wounds heal, but make certain they heal before the condition wears off, and pair it with a Numb spell if possible, because pain without respite takes its own toll. He has a card in his T'Ghee deck, The Open Wound. She teaches that all suffering leaves scars. So the condition scares him, and he says so in writing, for whoever reads the Cookbook next.
beats.gist: Allister writes in the Cookbook that The Open Wound card and immortality condition scare him.

beats.headline: A card made permanent
beats.text: Imani's eighth-floor card, Jacobus the Reverse Tooth Fairy, is out and buzzing in Carl's face. The notice says he is now permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card, due to something Carl did. Princess Donut did not know cards could be turned real. She and Carl are both thinking of Paz, whose card they ripped, and neither says it. Could Raul be set free? Carl doubts it. This was a god thing.
beats.gist: Jacobus the Reverse Tooth Fairy is permanently summoned and buzzing in Carl's face.

relations.note: Allister's edition was a T'Ghee deck

recap.text: The Cookbook manifests as a massive deck of T'Ghee playing cards for Allister, the author of the thirteenth edition. The game is a mix of chess and go fish. Allister spends hours studying the cards as part of a meditation-based religion.

Allister writes that his T'Ghee deck contains two vampiric forms representing death and the end of days. One is thirst-based evil, and the other is the Plague Bearer. Allister thinks the vampires on his floor are a combination of the two.

Squad leaders receive twenty flags to plant in creatures below five per cent health, turning them into T'Ghee totem cards. Sister Ines drives a flag into the neck of her dying friend Paz, turning him into a green common card. Carl rips the Paz card in half on his shoulder.

Allister writes in the Cookbook about the Immortality condition. He warns that wounds must heal before the condition wears off and suggests a Numb spell because pain without respite takes a toll. He holds a T'Ghee card called The Open Wound.

Imani's eighth-floor card, Jacobus the Reverse Tooth Fairy, buzzes in Carl's face. A notice states he is permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card. Carl and Princess Donut think of Paz, whose card they ripped, and Carl doubts Raul could be set free.

entities.name: Containment Interface
entities.role: Bootleg interface upgrade · the AI's failsafe

tagline.text: The Containment Interface was a neural enhancement hidden in a homeless man's frozen coffee. It gives access to the AI's containment, and to the fuse that would send the star at the centre of the system nova.
The Containment Interface has six tabs of numbers and a Fuse page with two of its five conditions met. The only other button Carl could press switched the containment off, and he pressed it.

beats.headline: Coffee, with a finger
beats.text: Christmas morning, in a shelter, in memory. Time stops, and Paulie delivers his real message. His coffee holds a neural enhancement: Crawler Carl pushes a finger into the frozen cup and drinks. It gives access to the AI containment, and upon it to what the Mantids call the fuse, a failsafe that trips when five or six conditions are met and sends the star at the centre of the system nova. The controller lets Carl pop it himself. He dies; so does everyone. It only works in a natural interface, and the AI, says Paulie, wants it done.
beats.gist: Carl drinks a neural enhancement from a frozen cup of coffee to access the AI containment.

beats.headline: Paulie's own opinion
beats.text: That was the pitch, Paulie says, the one he gives every day. Then the Paulie part of him speaks. Popping the fuse would disrupt the crawl for seasons, kill system leaders, and put the Mantids under a microscope. But the human in him hates wasting so many innocent lives, and direct action against the true culprits would be better. If you make this decision, be sure. It is more than a failsafe. It is the end of everything. Then a notice: Containment Interface is currently installing. A notification comes when the handshake is complete.
beats.gist: Paulie describes the Containment Interface as a failsafe that ends everything if the fuse pops.

beats.headline: So close to the edge
beats.text: Crawler Carl thinks of Lightning Lou, the old dog at the gas station in Florida left to spend Christmas Day alone. Carl curled up beside him on the floor and contemplated his options, and came so close to the edge that it almost broke his mind to think about it. Paulie's words come back to him: be sure it's your only option. On his chest, the eye blinks.
beats.gist: Carl thinks of Lightning Lou, an old dog at a Florida gas station alone on Christmas Day.

beats.headline: The handshake completes
beats.text: In Orren's zero zone, Carl asks whether Paulie ever made it into the dungeon. No, says Orren; most of them never do, and the parts of a collective mind are often disposable. Then the notice: Containment Interface is now available for use, as a new tab. Carl changes his request and asks to be sent to the gas station with the memory ghost of the dog, and sits beside Lightning Lou with a bag of chips and a soda. I could end it all right now, he thinks.
beats.gist: In Orren's zero zone, Carl learns the parts of a collective mind are often disposable.

beats.headline: Two buttons, one pressed
beats.text: There is no single Boom button. There are six tabs of numbers in a language that is not quite Syndicate standard, and the controls are for the device that installed the AI into the primal engine, not the AI itself. Carl screenshots everything. The Fuse page lists five benchmarks, two met, and a button: Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. At the end of a list sits the only other thing he can press: Disconnect Containment, which renders the failsafe inert.
